data.title: Out of control? France stunned by October 17 rioting
data.description: France didn't just erupt on Saturday – it exploded. Police were doubly overwhelmed by the turnout of the October 17 cost-of-living demonstrations, which saw two and-a-half times the crowds they expected. data.title: Amnesty on Turkish media crackdown: 'Disinformation flourishes when media landscape's narrowed down'
data.description: The state takeover of Halk TV, one of Turkey’s most widely watched news channels, represents far more than an isolated confrontation between the authorities and an independent broadcaster. For Milena Buyum, Amnesty International’s Turkey campaigner, it is part of a broader erosion of media pluralism, characterized by the appointment of state trustees, the detention of journalists and mounting restrictions on independent digital platforms. Buyum describes the intervention as a "brutal attack on media freedom in Turkey,” framing it within a sustained crackdown on independent journalism that has intensified since March 2025.

data.title: Zelensky says Starshield speed limits slowing down frontline response
data.description: Speed limits on a US military grade satellite system are hindering Ukrainian forces' ability to coordinate drone strikes against Russian forces, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday. Zelensky said frontline units had reported that the Starshield equipment "stops functioning at speeds of 130-160 kilometres (80-100 miles) per hour in various sectors of the front". Separately, a Ukrainian army brigade has announced the rescue of a wounded soldier from the front line using an aerial drone, describing the evacuation as the first of its kind. The brigade published a video showing the drone lowering itself to the ground, before a man in combat gear fastens himself to a winch onboard and is lifted upwards. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Ukraine.

data.title: ‘The last bastion is gone’: the US right idolised Orbán’s Hungary. Can they recover now he has fallen?
data.description: Over the past decade, Hungary has been a beacon for the ‘postliberal’ right, with pro-Trump thinkers making regular pilgrimages to Budapest. Now Orbán is gone, how will the movement adapt? A longer version of this article first appeared in The Drift Espresso Embassy, a third-wave coffee shop in Budapest’s diplomatic and governmental quarter, is where visiting reporters and academics come to talk politics. On the way in for my morning coffee on 18 March, I passed a poster for Viktor Orbán’s Fidesz party that had been vandalised with a marker pen: “the safe choice” had become “the certain way to get fucked”. From across the cafe, I spotted the American journalist and historian Anne Applebaum locked in conversation, possibly with a source. I heard someone exclaim: “Just like Mussolini!” It was election season in Hungary. It was also a couple of days before Cpac Hungary , a satellite event of the US-based conservative conference. As members of the international right arrived in town, the notorious Orbánist thinktank known as the Danube Institute was hosting an event called On Censorship, Tolerance, the Left and God. The official line would be: bad, good, bad, good. Continue reading...

data.title: Don’t be fooled. The AI that was supposed to save us time is doing just the opposite | Gaby Hinsliff
data.description: The government says it can transform the state with AI, but it is no match for the resulting stream of machine-generated slop. And we all pay the cost Another morning, another avalanche of emails. Even after a guilty cull, my inbox is sitting at well over 7,000, but lately I’ve started subscribing to the Quentin Crisp theory of housework: why bother, when after four years or so you stop noticing the accumulating dust? Empty inboxes just fill up again anyway. In theory, email was supposed to save hours of meetings, phone calls and standing over photocopiers. Instead, we just spend hours deleting stuff people wouldn’t have bothered telling us if it had meant picking up the phone, but which they can now spam to their entire database at the click of a button. The glorious ease and convenience of being able to reach the world in seconds came, we now know, with the inconvenience of them being able to reach you right back. Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Aberfan: The Village That Fought Back review – the contempt they have faced to get justice is sickening
data.description: As we witness the endless indignities these grieving families have endured in the six decades since the mining disaster, it is impossible not to turn red with rage ‘I’d like to have known her that bit longer, really. Those eight years went very, very quickly. I loved the child. I lost her. And that seemed to me to be the end of everything really, when she’d gone.” Ray Lee, now 90, lost his daughter Anne on 21 October 1966. It was the day her primary school, along with several surrounding houses, in Aberfan was engulfed by an estimated 100,000 tonnes of slurry from one of the colliery spoil tips that overshadowed the Welsh mining village. Anne was one of 116 children killed, alongside 28 adults. Continue reading...

data.title: Why terrorism laws stopped Sally Rooney selling books in the UK – podcast

Last year, Sally Rooney said she would be using her royalties to support Palestine Action, a group that is proscribed as a terrorist organisation under UK law. Since then, thousands of people have been arrested for supporting the group. Now, faced with the risk of prosecution under terrorism legislation, Rooney and her publishers have decided to stop supplying her books to retailers in the UK. Continue reading...

data.title: The ‘Finger cutter’ and the ‘Brazilian Escobar’: the men accused of bringing cocaine cartels to Europe
data.description: A Belgian criminal organisation’s links with a Brazilian cocaine gang have been the focus of a major trial in Brussels, where smuggling links have been alleged between European players and the drug cartels of Latin America In the early hours of 7 September, a convoy of heavily armed police swept through the sleeping streets of central Brussels towards the Haren district, on the city’s north-eastern outskirts. They made their way to 22 Avenue du Bourget, a militarised bunker-like complex that was the former headquarters of Nato. The modernist complex, with its austere and functional architecture, was hastily built in 1967 and houses the Justitia courtroom, where Belgium’s federal trials are now held. It was here that the perpetrators and accomplices of the 2015 Paris terrorist attacks and the 2016 Brussels attacks were tried in 2022. Continue reading...

The AI system was custom-built by experts at Mass General Brigham, a nonprofit, integrated academic healthcare system in Massachusetts, to estimate biological age and directly predict survival outcomes in patients diagnosed with cancer. data.title: ‘Crucial opportunity to act’ as study finds most of Europe’s wild bee species in decline
data.description: As Cop17 kicks off, records since 1921 show more bee species declining than increasing in all parts of Europe except the Alps Most of Europe’s wild bee species and about half of its hover fly species have declined over the last century, a study has found, as a UN biodiversity summit begins in Armenia. Records since 1921 show more bee species are declining than increasing in all parts of Europe except the Alpine region. The richness of bee and hover fly species suffered a persistent drop in the Atlantic and Continental regions, the study found, though trends in other regions were mixed or even positive. Continue reading...

data.title: In ruby-red Kansas, Trump contemplates the possibility of a Democratic win in the state
data.description: The president came out in support of Senator Roger Marshall, who is facing an unexpectedly strong challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton The fact that Donald Trump was here at all said more about a looming electoral disaster facing his Republican party next month than anything contained in his dark and discursive 98-minute stump speech. On Monday, amid raucous chants of “USA! USA!”, the president held his first campaign rally in Kansas for eight years. No Democrat has won a US Senate seat in this ruby-red state since 1932, the year Herbert Hoover was president, Amelia Earhart was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic and the Nazis became the biggest party in the German Reichstag. data.title: The CO2-absorbing building made of old sinks, windscreens and toilets: Ghent’s £17m design museum is a green marvel
data.description: Inspired by a gothic cathedral partly built using human bones, this gleaming monument to recycling boasts 62,000 bricks derived from construction waste – each made by the public during a two-day brick-making festival Museums often try to reflect the world around them, but rarely are they made so literally of their surroundings as the new design museum in Ghent . Rising above the Belgian city’s medieval tiled rooftops like an angular white watchtower, the new building has vacuumed up the city’s condemned concrete frames, windows, car windscreens, sinks and old toilets, and transformed them, phoenix-like, into a gleaming monument to recycling. “There’s nothing new about reuse,” says Andy Groarke, co-founder of Carmody Groarke , the London-based architects who designed the €20m (£17m) project with local firms Atama and Re-st . “We’ve just forgotten how to do it.” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It speaks very poorly of us as a society’: Lawrence Wright on his book on death row and redemption
data.description: The Pulitzer prize-winning writer’s new book looks at the women on death row in Texas and the nuns who have been trying to help them It is “stunning”, the Pulitzer-winning reporter Lawrence Wright said, that Redemption, his new book about women on death row in Texas and the nuns who minister to them, turns out to be published at a time of intense focus on capital punishment. Two cases dominate headlines: the Trump administration’s abandoned plan to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009, and Tennessee’s failure to kill the convicted murderer Christa Pike by lethal injection. Away from the headlines, in Texas and elsewhere, executions continue . Continue reading...

data.title: Excessive wealth, extreme emissions – and ecocide: what I learned at Europe’s big superyacht show
data.description: These yachts are highly popular with the ‘super-bourgeoisie’ – and getting bigger. Can anything be done to stop them destroying our seas? Who knew? Apparently everyone did, apart from me: you don’t wear shoes on a superyacht. Now, about to step on to my first teak deck at the Monaco Yacht Show, I’ve got to take my trainers off, and I’m having a sock panic. Have they got holes? Do they even match? Do they smell? To be honest, I’ve come dressed all wrong for Europe’s big annual superyacht trade exhibition. The code for men seems to be crisp and tucked in, blazers and chinos, navy and white, sculpted hair and designer sunnies. (I went colourful, loose, casual). For women, it’s something like Riviera elegance. Everyone – whether they’re Italian, French, English, German, American, exhibitors, buyers, brokers, charterers – seems to know each other. The international superyacht community seems to be a close-knit one, and I’m not part of it. Yet. Continue reading...

data.title: Hollywood AI-listers: is the technology ready to rival flesh-and-blood film stars?
data.description: As a freaky Val Kilmer doppelganger stars in a new western and faux starlet Tilly Norwood is set for her feature debut, experts are split on whether mainstream adoption is a long way down the line – or just around the corner ‘Don’t fear the dead – and don’t fear me.” An exact facsimile of a young Val Kilmer, not quite dead and not quite alive, utters that baiting line in the trailer for the new western As Deep as the Grave. Director Coerte Voorhees knows exactly what he is doing – this is an AI-created version of the late actor, approved by his family but bringing with it a heap of controversy about whether such technology could make flesh-and-blood thespians redundant. Not just yet, judging by the extended glimpse of the film released earlier this year : it looks like a thirtysomething Kilmer, if a robot version had been sent back to the 1920s American wilderness by Skynet and, as well as being strangely rigid, had forgotten to download his voice, let alone his signature air of spacey shrewdness. Kilmer’s estate signed off on it, citing his enthusiasm for new technology that expands storytelling, but surely he would have been dismayed by this freaky doppelganger. Continue reading...

data.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the maggots that rained down like hail
data.description: The record-breaking heat in London, in summer 2022, resulted in an appalling problem in my neighbourhood – which one man took on, armed only with a jet wash It was that terrifying summer in 2022 when London reached 40C. I was staying in a friend’s flat while she was away for a year, a former housing association property where the living room ceiling permanently had a hole in it. Each day, the air felt thicker and the leaves looked more limp. Dust clung to every surface. With no wind, the stench of the bins lingered. I’d nicknamed the guy next door “Techno Guy” because his life’s great pleasure appeared to be sitting in the driver’s seat of a parked red convertible, stereo on full volume, revving the engine but going nowhere. Maybe it was to preserve his car battery, maybe it was to get away from his wife. His music genre of choice, Shazam told me, was Romanian techno (though he was also fond of the Cher megamix). He smoked constantly, each drag like a first breath. The sound of him hawking up phlegm in the morning became a kind of alarm clock. Continue reading...

data.title: Alone With a Book by Tessa Hadley review – an acclaimed writer’s cultural prescription
data.description: This collection of essays from the beloved novelist is full of gem-like insights on art and books When Tessa Hadley was a child, someone gave her a copy of Lois Lenski’s Papa Small, which follows Mr Small and his family through a typical week. Papa Small goes to work, Mama Small cooks the supper, and the small Smalls dry and put away the dishes. “I thrilled to its ordinariness,” writes Hadley, a novelist known for her depictions of the ordinary that are anything but. In all her novels and short stories, she’s spectacularly alive to the everyday, both the seemingly humdrum surfaces and the darkest emotional depths. So you know what you’re in for when you reach for a book by Hadley, which is why I was in equal parts excited and apprehensive about her first foray into nonfiction. At least, it’s her first in bound form: Alone With a Book comprises published essays written since 2000. A nimble mix of biography, cultural criticism and personal reflection, it traces her development as both a reader and a writer, and burrows into the literary and artistic works that have kept her company along the way. For fans, it’s a fascinating insight into how and why she became the beloved author she is. For the rest, it’s a first-class reading (and picture) list. Continue reading...

data.title: Do not be distracted by global crises. Nature cannot wait for a better year – we must act now | Steven Guilbeault
data.description: In 2022, I helped push through the international agreement to protect biodiversity. Wars and economic pressures can make nature seem like a ‘nice-to-have’. But it is a critical asset, and Cop17 must deliver real action When I was five, property developers came to cut down the woods behind my home in La Tuque, Quebec. My mother encouraged me to climb one of the trees in protest, then told the developers, straight-faced, that there was nothing she could do when they asked her to get me down. A few days later, the tree was cut down anyway. I thought about that tree in the early hours of a freezing Montreal morning in December 2022, as the gavel came down on a global agreement between nearly 200 countries to halt and reverse the loss of nature by 2030. I thought about how important nature is for our health, our food security and our economies, but also how much passion there is around protecting it, and how it has the power to inspire people all around the world. Continue reading...

data.title: Political hate speech can have real-world fallout. After the alleged attack on Helen Haines, our leaders must act | Paul Daley
data.description: Social media amplify the worst excesses of what passes for public discourse, while some media outlets foment polarisation If the increasingly vituperative tenor of our public discourse, online and verbal, has fully trailed America’s into the murky dungeon of political violence with the appalling alleged attack on Helen Haines, Australia’s political class has only itself to blame. Amid outpourings of concern from across the political spectrum (including from people who have fostered considerable vicious personal animus online and in the parliament) for the gravely injured and much-respected member for Indi , it is blindingly evident that the political square has long been utterly incapable of self-regulation. data.title: Shall we have another EU referendum? Maybe – but not yet | Polly Toynbee
data.description: We saw last time what reckless reliance on close polling led to. The omertà on rejoining has now been broken, but it would be folly to move too soon When I hear that word again, a shudder runs down my spine. I want to groan, hold my head in my hands and wail. The horror! No, never again, not another referendum. But the idea is back in play as Andy Burnham looks for ways to reverse a decade of economic stagnation. As the prime minister dared to unlock the door to a Brussels reunion, you could hear Ode to Joy burst out from all remainers. But the prospect of a re-run of the most self-destructive vote in our history is dismaying. Polly Toynbee is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on France’s protests: a polarised country is in a perilous political moment | Editorial
data.description: The scenes of social unrest and violence at the weekend are an ominous portent, ahead of elections which may deliver a far-right presidency In Emmanuel Macron’s book Revolution , published ahead of the 2017 presidential election that he went on to win, he promised to restore hope to a country that was losing faith in its future. As Mr Macron’s lame-duck second term enters its last phase against a quasi-insurrectionary backdrop of torched public buildings and looted shops, the failure of that political project appears total. The worst scenes of urban violence for years overshadowed a weekend of protest that gravely undermined what is left of the French president’s authority. As police lost control of the streets, more than 2,000 shops were ransacked. Far-left groups targeted town halls and local buildings, and engaged in pitched battles with the police, whose disastrously heavy-handed response to last week’s high school protests has succeeded only in escalating tensions. data.title: The Guardian view on Trump and Putin: Ukraine’s future is not theirs to bargain away | Editorial
data.description: Russia wants America and China to decide Ukraine’s future without Kyiv. Europe must challenge this dangerous return to diplomacy of the strong for the strong Does Vladimir Putin know exactly how to play Donald Trump? The history of chummy phone calls, high-profile meetings and attempts to bring Russia in from the cold certainly suggests that Moscow’s thuggish ruler has a hold on this American president. If Mr Trump agrees to negotiate Ukraine’s future with Mr Putin and China’s Xi Jinping without Ukraine at the table, he will have handed the Russian leader a victory before talks begin. The message will be that strongmen are ruling the world and determining the fate of weaker nations. Ukraine has the right to determine its future. That right cannot be waved away by a self-serving Russian proposal, however much it indulges Mr Trump’s belief that world affairs should be settled by powerful men. The scales are falling from European eyes. Trumpian America is raising doubts about whether it will help deter aggression or even honour its Nato commitments. If Washington now rewards Moscow and pressures Ukraine to accept a raw deal, it would be a betrayal . European governments would wonder where America might be in the future when their own security is threatened. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Villarreal’s Iñigo Pérez ready to meet Iraola again in test of old bond
data.description: Refused a work permit at Bournemouth, Pérez comes face to face with Liverpool’s head coach in Champions League On Iñigo Pérez’s first day as a head coach he took a call from Andoni Iraola, just as he had every day for months. They had known each other for 22 years, lived in the same residency, come through the same academy and played in the same team; they had worked side by side, manager and assistant, and embarked on an adventure together. Now, though, Pérez was having to go it alone. At 36, he had become what his friend thought he would be from the moment they met, just not so soon. “He wished me luck and said he was there for me,” Pérez said, “said that if I ever needed anything …” Well, maybe not anything . data.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
data.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

data.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
data.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

data.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
data.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

data.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
data.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

data.title: Houthi attack kills 53 in biggest single loss of life since Yemen civil war reignited
data.description: More than 200 mostly young people said to be injured after ballistic missile attack on training camp for government forces At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September. The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and was described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government. The injured were taken from the police and army training camp in the Jardan district to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were made. Continue reading...

data.title: Four years ago countries made a historic deal to save nature. Is it dead in the water?
data.description: So far not a single target of the plan has been met. As negotiators convene for Cop17, the pressure is on to find a way to honour the commitments made at previous summits Cop17 at a glance: everything you need to know about the UN’s nature summit Passersby could smell the dead fish before they saw them. In August, more than 3,000 pike, roach, carp and rudd were found lifeless along the River Wensum in Norwich. Some gasped for air in their final moments, desperate for the oxygen that heatwave conditions had depleted in the water. Investigators believe that the die-off was triggered by heavy rainfall that flushed through high concentrations of pollution at a time when wildlife were already struggling. The 45-mile (70km) chalk river is one of about 250 in the country. They are a geological accident almost unique to Britain – and one of Earth’s rarest habitats. They emerge from chalk aquifers and are home to species such as freshwater shrimp, otters and stoneflies, also providing drinking water for millions of people. But just 11 have formal protection, with many ravaged by sewage pollution and overextraction. The Norfolk river is one of the few that does have legal protection, but it is in poor ecological health. Continue reading...

data.title: Melting Ron DeSantis statue unveiled to call out his inaction on climate crisis
data.description: Florida governor has consistently opposed any legislation to curb planet-heating emissions, calling it a ‘radical climate agenda’ A life-sized statue of Ron DeSantis, the Florida governor, was unveiled and promptly began melting in front of an audience in Tallahassee in a symbolic protest at his rejection of action on the climate crisis. The silvery statue, revealed to an audience of onlookers last week, melted away to show a skull under DeSantis’s face. The structure was cast from solid gallium, a metal that melts at 85.6F (29.8C), which is below summertime high temperatures frequently reached in Tallahassee, Florida’s capital. Continue reading...

data.title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
data.description: Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in Greece In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system. The category 2 hurricane remained roughly 100 miles (160km) south-west of the coast of Mexico, meaning the worst of the conditions stayed offshore. However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday. Rainfall totals of 100-150mm were likely for these areas, prompting warnings of flooding and landslides. Warnings also covered the risk of a dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas of onshore winds across the coast of south-western Mexico. By Monday morning, Trudy had weakened and been downgraded to a tropical storm, with coastal warnings being lifted. Continue reading...

data.title: She was harassed for crude remarks about Modi at a Cockroach protest. Now she can’t leave home
data.description: ​After a protest clip went viral, a teenager’s life was torn apart by threats that sent her and her family into hiding. Plus, a book on citizen journalism Before 24 July, a person I will call R was preoccupied with the ordinary routines of teenage life: experimenting with makeup, grumbling over mathematics homework and hanging out with friends at a tea stall. data.title: Gilgamesh by Simon Armitage review – an ancient epic is brilliantly translated for our times
data.description: The poet laureate’s visceral take on the legendary Mesopotamian hero’s wild adventures is a tour de force The poet laureate is paid a salary of £5,750 per annum plus a barrel of sherry. No specific duties are attached to the role, but there is an expectation that poets will write verse for public occasions and royal events, a duty that Simon Armitage has fulfilled by writing a poem on the death of Elizabeth II, Floral Tribute, and another to mark the coronation of Charles and Camilla in 2023. Though it’s an awkward time for the royals, no laureate is going to write about them behaving badly (it wasn’t John Dryden, the first laureate, who wrote about Charles II’s bedroom habits, but John Wilmot, Earl of Rochester). And yet with Gilgamesh, Armitage does deliver a poem about royalty’s misdeeds, at least in part. The epic originated in ancient Mesopotamia (modern-day Iraq) at least 4,000 years ago, and it begins with the eponymous demigod, king of Uruk, lording it over his subjects. Among other bad habits, he exercises the “right of the first night”, which allows him to bed newlywed brides before their husbands. To check his powers, the gods create his counterpart, the wild man Enkidu, who confronts Gilgamesh outside the house of one of these brides. The two rivals turned comrades then embark on a series of extraordinary adventures, including battles with Humbaba, guardian of the Cedar Forest, and with the winged Bull of Heaven, sent by the goddess Ishtar in revenge after Gilgamesh rejects her marriage proposal. Following Enkidu’s death, Gilgamesh sets out alone on a desperate quest for immortality that leads him to the very edge of the world. Continue reading...

data.title: Secrets, lies and a shock A-list cameo: how You Can See Everything became the film of the year
data.description: Nathan Fielder’s secretive Elizabeth Holmes documentary has become a sold-out smash hit and might make Oscars history Spoilers ahead If there is one moment that sums up You Can See Everything , the new A24 documentary on Elizabeth Holmes that until this weekend was shrouded in spoiler-averse secrecy, it is, perhaps surprisingly, the one everyone already knows: co-director Nathan Fielder, the droll comedian known for deadpanning subjects into submission, sitting eye to eye with Holmes, the unblinking fabulist of Theranos infamy. In tight zoom, saturation turned up – Fielder’s arched brows and Holmes’s oceanic blue eyes as stark as two magnetic poles – he asks her: “Are you being real right now?” That question hangs over much of the colossal three-hour movie, particularly a claustrophobic first half that has made headlines since the film’s existence was announced in September. That first half – essentially, the only part of the movie anyone respecting spoiler guidelines and/or the theatrical experience could talk about – takes place entirely in 2023, when Fielder and his co-director Lance Oppenheim, along with a small crew, embedded with Holmes, her husband, Billy Evans, and their two small children in the run-up to her prison sentence for fraud. We watch as Fielder, over a few surreal weeks in a beachfront rental, attempts to puncture Holmes’s indomitable facade of faultlessness. It’s not exactly comedic, this chess game between three norms-ignoring people, but it can be quite funny: TV’s grand illusionist, an absurdist auteur who will go as far as actually obtaining a 737 pilot’s license for the bit, stymied by a world-class fabricator, with her poorly dissembling husband on the side. This section resembles, in feel, the pull of an internet wormhole: the closer you zoom in on a subject, without outside context, the more sense devolves. Was Holmes “being real”, for instance, when she told Fielder, with seemingly complete sincerity, that she has never told a lie in her life ? Or when she continued to insist, despite plain reality, that Theranos devices could perform 1,000 diagnostic tests? Continue reading...

data.title: How we made Come Dine With Me: ‘Someone served sushi off a guy’s naked chest!’
data.description: ‘We’re not there to humiliate or to sneer. Channel 4 insisted everyone had to be a decent cook – the threshold was that contestants had to know what coriander was’ It all started in the early 00s when I tried to throw a dinner party. I was an executive producer during the early days of reality TV – and a house-proud young mum. My posh cousin and her even posher husband came for a meal. I was rushing to get the kids to bed and tidy up, so the food was an afterthought. I’d never made couscous before but decided to serve it with chicken. It was awful. Dry chicken with congealed couscous. At one point, my cousin’s husband stuck his fork in this rock-solid lump, lifted it up and said: “What actually is this?” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘They pulled a guy’s face off. It’s my favourite bit!’ Linda Cardellini on Freaks and Geeks, Mad Men and slasher horror Crystal Lake
data.description: She got to torment Don Draper in Mad Men and has just won an Emmy for DTF St Louis. But nothing prepared the star for all the gore as she switched to horror with the Friday the 13th prequel ‘The first time I had the tooth in my hand,” says Linda Cardellini, “I thought, ‘Oh my God, this is what I’m doing.’” The star of Freaks and Geeks, ER, Dead to Me, Mad Men and DTF St Louis (for which she recently won an Emmy) is talking about her pivot towards full-blown horror. In Crystal Lake, the prequel to the Friday the 13th movies, Cardellini plays Pamela Voorhees, the original slasher of the 1980 film. The tooth, by the way, is human and gets embedded in Pam’s knuckle – until she yanks it out with a gruesome, revolting slurping sound. Casual filmgoers may associate Friday the 13th with Jason, the hockey-mask-wearing serial killer. But aficionados will know that Pam, Jason’s mother, is the villain of the first movie. “He didn’t even have the mask until the third movie,” says Cardellini, who has clearly done her homework. “Pam is the original killer, in vengeance of his death.” (There is some massaging of previous storylines in Crystal Lake, such as moving Jason’s drowning from the 1950s to the early 70s, but since the franchise is flexible enough to have sent Jason into space at one point, a bit of timeline tweaking feels fair game.) Continue reading...

data.title: Monster Mia review – kooky kid discovers school of beastly besties in wholesome Halloween fun
data.description: A scrappy girl discovers her tribe – which includes a vegan vampire – at a school for top scarers in this entertaining pre-teen animation In films, twins are usually written as either identical personalities or complete and total opposites, and it’s the latter dynamic that’s at work in this pre-teen animation. One twin is a popular straight-A student heavily invested in fitting in and doing well at ballet, while her sister Mia is a chaotic kook. They both live in Primrose, an appropriately named community that apparently used to be infested with monsters, but can now claim to be proudly monster-free for the last 500 years. The twins’ parents are supportive of their golden child and try their best to understand Mia too, but it is easier for them to praise the kid bringing home the perfect behaviour reports than the one exasperating her teachers with her determination to discover monsters, by hook or by crook. Scrappy Mia is, naturally, the protagonist of this film, and it’s not too long before she finds herself accidentally enrolled in Rotwood Academy, a school for monsters who would be shocked to discover a human in their midst; from their point of view, humans are brutal, cold-blooded creatures, best avoided, who prefer – ugh! – cupcakes to grave-worms. Mia quickly buddies up with some misfits including a vegan vampire, and the stage is thus set for some Addams Family Lite hijinks, with culture clash comedy highlighting the difference between monster norms and human ways providing much of the humour. Continue reading...

data.title: Pedigree chums: why the movies are killing off fewer dogs
data.description: Are film-makers wary of alienating increasingly sensitive audiences by offing a pooch? Or is humanity now just too soft to deal with the trauma of a Turner & Hooch? Revenge, dog gets shot. Turner & Hooch, dog gets shot. Red, dog gets shot. Man with the Gun, dog gets shot. Badlands, dog gets shot. Dog Soldiers, you’ll never guess. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘We tried to levitate the Pentagon’: the almost unbelievable life of Ed Sanders, trickster god of the US counterculture
data.description: He gave Jimi Hendrix his gear, freaked out Frank Sinatra, inspired Norman Mailer – and tried to topple the American war machine. As a documentary about his band the Fugs comes out, the 87-year-old gives a rare interview “Charles Manson once wrote me a letter saying, ‘If I was as powerful as you claim then you wouldn’t be here,’” Ed Sanders tells me over a video call, savouring the menace in that sentence. Sanders is an American maverick; a musician, poet, activist, journalist and author whose greatest hit remains his bestselling 1971 book The Family, in which he chronicled the lives, crimes and trials of Manson and his followers. Sanders was well placed to report on crazed hippies, having played a pivotal role in launching the US counterculture – though he very much espoused peace, love and consciousness-raising, rather than Manson’s apocalyptic worldview. Continue reading...

data.title: Life Out of Order by Audrey Niffenegger review – does this sequel measure up to The Time Traveler’s Wife?
data.description: More than two decades on, the passion that ignited Niffenegger’s debut has all but evaporated from this confused follow-up I run a reading workshop which begins with a little shelf assessment. Participants bring a stack of books that have shaped who they are: childhood treasures; new revelations; comfort reads. Books they once cherished but have now outgrown. The usual suspect in that category is Audrey Niffenegger’s 2003 novel The Time Traveler’s Wife . Once smitten, readers now find that time-warped romance cruel. What felt like destiny now feels like a cage. As they explain, I’m always struck by the same thought: Wasn’t it always cruel? Wasn’t that the point? Henry DeTamble and Clare Abshire are a couple caught in a causal loop. The irresolvable question is where that loop starts: does a bright young art student fall in love with a junior librarian, or does a time-travelling man groom a child to become his future wife? If the answer is both – and it has to be – what are we to make of their marriage? Can you truly choose someone if you believe the choice is already made? Continue reading...

data.title: Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History by Benjamin Moser review – the deep roots of a contemporary movement
data.description: A biographer’s affecting account of prominent critics of Zionism, from Hannah Arendt to Nan Goldin “Everyone in America – at least as far as I knew – was a Zionist,” recalls Benjamin Moser, “especially but not only if you were Jewish.” A Pulitzer-winning biographer of Susan Sontag, he remembers being brought up short in his 20s, when a friend described Israel as “a bunch of foreigners who had no business in the Middle East” and Zionism as a “terrible mistake”. Moser, who recently turned 50, admits: “I was not even aware that Zionism was controversial.” The shift in perspective culminated in a visit to the occupied territories in 2016, during which he found “the reality of the occupation of Palestine … deranging”. His new book includes 12 portraits of Jewish figures who have opposed Zionism, a movement formed in the late 19th century to advocate for the creation of a homeland for Jewish people in Palestine. It is contentious to oppose Zionism today, but Moser wants contemporary Jewish activists to “feel less alone” by showing that debates about Zionism were once mainstream in Jewish communal life. While around 90% of American Jews now support Israel’s right to exist as a Jewish state (although fewer identify as Zionists), fewer than 1% belonged to the largest American Zionist organisation in 1914. The first character study is of Rabbi Aaron Samuel Tamares, who thought that Judaism offered a vision of a world beyond the devastating nationalism of the first world war. The book closes with a moving account of the photographer Nan Goldin, who spoke out, at considerable cost, as the assault on Gaza began in 2023 following the October 7th attacks. Continue reading...

data.title: With nine new recordings of Mahler’s epic Resurrection Symphony this year alone, which rises above the rest?
data.description: The second – the ‘Resurrection’ – was the first Mahler symphony ever to be recorded, and it is still today an essential work in any conductor’s catalogue. But with hundreds of recordings, from Ormandy to Bernstein and Rattle, which does our reviewer recommend? Is it something in the water? Or is it simply that triumph over adversity sells in today’s uncertain world? Whatever the reason, Mahler’s Resurrection Symphony has already received four major UK performances this year: a season finale for the BBC Philharmonic in Manchester, a season opener for both the City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra and the London Symphony Orchestra , and an 80th season celebratory concert for the Philharmonia Orchestra in London . Next month the London City Orchestra perform it in Croydon’s Fairfield Halls. On disc, the field of Mahler 2s is even more crowded. Apple Music Classical currently throws up 222 listings; Presto Music ’s search engine returns 260 results, many of them complete recordings to download or buy on CD or vinyl (some of these, of course, are reissues of recognised classic accounts). Continue reading...

data.title: A Zack Snyder DC Universe might not have been such a bad thing, after all
data.description: After Joss Whedon’s arrival, back in the news with comments from Ben Affleck, the franchise lost a sense of earnest passion that could have sustained a weary DCEU Nine years after superhero epic Justice League arrived in cinemas, there ought to be very little left to say about how it all went wrong. Zack Snyder shot the film, Joss Whedon substantially rewrote and reshot it, and audiences eventually got to see both men’s versions. Any debate over their relative merits long ago disappeared. Whedon is pretty much cancelled; Snyder has reinvented himself as the writer-director of extremely average ersatz Star Wars movies for Netflix, and an entirely new DC universe is under way that has very little to do with either of them. To a greater or lesser extent, the world has moved on. But Ben Affleck’s latest comments raise an uncomfortable question about whether Snyder’s departure was ever presented honestly. Speaking to Josh Horowitz on the Happy Sad Confused podcast , Affleck, who played Batman, described the Justice League reshoots as the lowest point of his career, but reserved his strongest criticism for the circumstances of Snyder’s departure. The director stepped away in May 2017 , two months after his daughter Autumn killed herself, aged 20, with the public explanation that he needed to be with his family. Affleck, however, alleged that studio Warner Bros had used the tragedy to justify replacing him. “The way in which that was, I thought, used as an excuse was one of the shittiest things I’ve ever seen,” Affleck said. “It was so gross.” Continue reading...

Affleck, however, alleged that studio Warner Bros had used the tragedy to justify replacing him. “The way in which that was, I thought, used as an excuse was one of the shittiest things I’ve ever seen,” Affleck said. “It was so gross.” Continue reading...

data.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Orlando was paralysed and almost died – then became the perfect guide dog
data.description: He had tetanus and I was brokenhearted when it seemed as if he wouldn’t pull through. But he worked hard, made a full recovery and helped to change someone’s life When I first met Orlando, he was about eight weeks old. I’m a puppy raiser for the charity Guide Dogs ; the puppies come to live with us in Swanley, Kent, until they are 12 to 18 months old. I started training him, but one day, I noticed he was shaking his head, which can mean there is something wrong with a dog’s ears. We took him to the vet and, on the second visit, we were told to rush him straight to the Royal Veterinary hospital because he had tetanus. Dogs aren’t vaccinated against tetanus because it is so rare, and I don’t think I realised how unwell Orlando was. For the first week it was terrifying. He became completely paralysed and I was awake every night expecting a call to say that he had died. He was too sick to carry on training as a guide dog. He had to learn how to eat, walk and do almost everything again. Continue reading...

data.title: Nashville held a developer's permit for years over a future road; appeals court revives lawsuit

The court's decision enables the developer's claims to progress to judicial review, potentially influencing other property owners experiencing similar challenges.

data.title: Kentucky sinks 1,700 discarded Christmas trees in a lake to create homes for fish

data.title: This Cold War missile silo in Kansas plunges 182 feet underground; its converted command centre is now a home listed for $1.6 million
data.description: A former missile silo in Kansas is listed for sale at $1.6 million after conversion. The property includes 2,500 square feet of livable space and a 182-foot silo. Originally built for military purposes, this site has modern amenities like high-speed internet. Future possibilities for the property include conference venues or residential condominiums. Buyers must consider the unique maintenance requirements of this underground structure before purchase.

data.description: A contentious legal battle has arisen between Xcel Energy and the Dickey family regarding land essential for renewable energy initiatives. Xcel is contesting a recent ruling that restricts its eminent domain authority for an easement in Colorado. The conflict primarily revolves around fair compensation and proposed power line routes that impact the family's agricultural endeavors.

data.title: Oklahoma’s 1938 Art Deco landmark reopens after $70 million restoration
data.description: Oklahoma's recent $70 million enhancement of the Jim Thorpe Memorial Office Building marks a significant achievement. This renovation not only modernizes the infrastructure but also respects the impressive Art Deco aesthetics. With four state agencies set to operate within, accessibility to public services will improve. The introduction of public art further ties the building to Jim Thorpe's Olympic history, demonstrating a perfect blend of contemporary needs and rich heritage.

data.title: China Alleges US Ship Incursion: Navy says warship entered Sabina Shoal without consent; US yet to respond
data.description: The USS Charleston has come under fire from China's Southern Theater Command Navy for allegedly trespassing into contested waters near Sabina Shoal. This area is embroiled in claims from both China and the Philippines, adding complexity to the situation. In response, the Chinese navy reported mobilizing its forces to keep a close watch on the USS Charleston, perceiving its presence as a possible threat to maritime stability.

data.title: A New York entrepreneur turns high-protein lupini bean pizzas into a $700,000 business
data.description: In January 2025, Damiano Messineo introduced Loopini, a unique high-protein pizza crafted from lupini beans. By mid-2026, the brand had made impressive strides, moving from a single location in New York City to partnerships with large retailers such as Whole Foods and Target. Messineo's 100-day product testing during his Ironman training paid off, with Loopini achieving $700,000 in revenue by April 2026 and eyeing future national expansion while prioritizing quality.

data.title: 'US is acting as international delinquent': Why Cuba and America clashed at UN
data.description: During a heated United Nations discussion on human rights, tensions flared between the US and Cuba. US ambassador Mike Waltz accused Cuban diplomats of persecuting dissidents, while Cuban ambassador Ernesto Soberón Guzmán argued that US sanctions inflicted major hardships on ordinary Cubans. This clash occurs just ahead of a critical UN General Assembly vote concerning the ongoing US trade embargo against Cuba, an issue intertwined with Cuba's deep economic crisis.

data.title: Barber Detains Alleged Attacker: Local overpowers man accused of ramming MP; probe eyes political violence
data.description: In a harrowing incident in Australia, barber Ricky Jefferies sprang into action after hearing a loud crash. He rushed outside to find lawmaker Helen Haines badly hurt following a vehicle collision. Jefferies bravely disarmed the assailant by removing a knife and held him until authorities arrived. Haines remains in critical condition post-surgery, and the situation has prompted an investigation involving counterterrorism teams due to fears of political violence.

data.title: Saudi Arabia executes 2 Bangladeshis over ‘indecent acts’ in a Mecca mosque
data.description:
Saudi Arabia has executed two Bangladeshi nationals, a man and a woman, after they were convicted of committing “indecent acts” in a mosque in the Muslim holy city of Mecca.
Bangladesh said it was not informed before the sentences were carried out and has sought information from Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi Interior Ministry said the Bangladeshis were executed because of “the gravity and seriousness of their actions in violating the sanctity of both time and place”.
It did not elaborate.

data.title: Au Canada, la province de l’Alberta vote contre son indépendance

data.title: A defesa da democracia começa dentro das nossas casas
data.description: Domingo, 4 de outubro. Acordei às 5h e, às 7h15, saí de casa para votar. Às 7h22, já estava na fila. Cinco minutos depois, uma moça perguntou: "Quem quer acompanhar a zerésima?". "Eu quero!", respondi, levantando a mão. Subi as escadas em direção à minha seção. Às 7h34, acompanhei a emissão da zerésima, que comprova que não havia votos registrados na urna antes do início da votação. Exatamente às 8h, fui a primeira a votar na minha seção. Leia mais (10/19/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: Vitória de Lula ou de Flávio não leva ao mesmo 2030
data.description: O debate a que assistimos no domingo foi deprimente, mas não surpreendente. É o resultado esperado do clima de constante alarmismo e polarização afetiva que domina a política nacional. Flávio puxou a disputa para a lama das acusações mútuas; Lula caiu e não saíram mais dali. Há controvérsias sobre quem "venceu". Mais do que favorecer um ou outro, aquele espetáculo deprimente deve ter, isso, sim, fortalecido em muitos a convicção de que nossa política está perdida e de que nunca descemos tão baixo. Esse sentimento desmobiliza a participação política, tende à abstenção e, portanto, prejudica a estratégia de Lula de levar mais gente às urnas . Mas imagino que também fortaleça o desejo de que, algum dia, de algum jeito, o cenário político mude. Leia mais (10/19/2026 - 21h32)

data.title: Daniel Helldén får riksdagsarvode – och över 20 000 i pension från Stockholms stad

data.title: DN Debatt. ”President Trump agerar faktiskt helt rationellt”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Världen kommer inte att återgå till det normala när Donald Trump lämnar Vita huset. Det ”normala” finns inte kvar. Trump är heller inte allmäktig skapare av vår nya världsordning. När vi kritiserar hans agerande är det inte bara presidenten vi kämpar mot, utan hela den moderna världens barnsliga logik, skriver Søren Schultz Hansen, gästforskare vid Syddansk universitet.

data.title: Förhöjd säkerhet – när Israel spelar i Borås: ”Finns en hotbild”
data.description: Att ett israeliskt flicklandslag i fotboll spelar veckans EM-kvalturnering i Borås har väckt debatt. data.title: Trots fängelsedomen – Bolsonaro kan ta makten via sin son
data.description: Högernationalisten Jair Bolsonaro var både älskad och hatad i Brasilien. Som president gjorde han sig känd för att skövla regnskog och motsätta sig covidvaccin. När han döms till fängelse efter ett försök till statskupp är det ett dråpslag för hans kontroversiella rörelse. Men ett år senare har han återuppstått politiskt – genom sin son. Inför Brasiliens presidentval på söndag har den nya kandidaten Flávio Bolsonaro använt en AI-version av sin far på valmöten, och lyckats locka landets fattiga genom drastiska förslag om att skjuta gängmedlemmar.

data.title: Elżbieta Łukacijewska: UE myśli o ograniczeniu Airbnb. W tle kryzys mieszkaniowy
data.description: Wysokie czynsze, rosnące ceny nieruchomości, wieloletnie oczekiwanie na lokal – to niektóre z problemów, z którymi muszą radzić sobie miliony Europejczyków we wszystkich państwach członkowskich UE. Komisja Europejska zaproponowała projekt rozporządzenia w sprawie mieszkań dostępnych cenowo, który ma ułatwić władzom krajowym i lokalnym reagowanie na kryzys mieszkaniowy, m.in. tam, gdzie najem krótkoterminowy ogranicza dostępność lokali.

data.title: Desítky tisíc lidí musí letos vyměnit řidičák. Nejvíc ve Středočeském kraji a Praze
data.description: Už téměř tři roky u sebe nemusí řidiči v Česku vozit řidičský průkaz. To ale neznamená, že onu plastovou kartičku, i když leží třeba na dně šuplíku, mohou nechat propadnout. Majitelé dokladů si musí hlídat dobu platnosti a včas požádat o výměnu. Podle zprávy, kterou Ministerstvo dopravy zveřejnilo počátkem října, čeká letos výměna přes dvě stě tisíc lidí.

data.title: V rolích bojoval s vnitřními běsy i pocitem viny. Se Štěpničkou se loučí plné divadlo
data.description: V úterý se v pražském Národním divadle koná poslední rozloučení s Jiřím Štěpničkou. Nad rakví promluvil ředitel Jan Burian a herec Vladislav Beneš. Dále vystoupí Taťjana Medvecká či Igor Orozovič. Dění v divadle můžete sledovat v přímém přenosu na iDNES.cz. Herec a dabér zemřel 11. října ve věku 79 let.

data.title: Alberta zůstane kanadská. Proti odtržení provincie bylo přes 70 procent voličů
data.description: Voliči v kanadské provincii Alberta v pondělním referendu odmítli zahájit proces odtržení od Kanady, proti bylo asi 76 procent hlasujících. Premiér Mark Carney tak obhájil svou politiku v době obchodní války Kanady se Spojenými státy. Výsledek odpovídá průzkumům veřejného mínění, podle nichž podpora odtržení této na ropu bohaté kanadské provincie dlouhodobě nepřesahuje 25 procent.

data.title: Jako by věděl o výročí Medvídka Pú. Huňáč vlezl do knihovny a sežral sklenici medu
data.description: Jako by si chtěl výročí ověřit přímo u zdroje. Právě 14. října, přesně sto let od prvního vydání knihy Medvídek Pú Alana Alexandera Milnea, se do knihovny v kalifornském Mammoth Lakes vydal skutečný medvěd černý. Na otevírací dobu přitom nečekal – dovnitř se dostal už kolem šesté ráno. Knihovníci později žertovali, že nový chlupatý „knihovník“ možná přišel hledat právě výtisk Púa.

data.title: Izraelci jsou čím dál víc odříznutí od světa.  Teď musí i řešit, s kým letět, aby doletěli
data.description: Poslední týdny se na izraelské nebe vrátilo více aerolinek, ale stále děsí terorismus i další válka. Izraelci tak musí řešit, s kým letět, aby doletěli. data.title: Východ Česka zasáhne silný vítr, nárazy budou až 90 kilometrů za hodinu
data.description: Meteorologové varují před silným větrem, který zasáhne část Moravy a Slezska. Výstraha platí od dnešního večera do středečního večera, uvedl Český hydrometeorologický ústav. Vítr může na horách v nárazech dosáhnout rychlosti až 90 kilometrů v hodině, což je síla vichru.

data.title: Ruské drony útočily u Kyjeva, několik lidí zabily. Ukrajinci udeřili u ropovodu Družba
data.description: Nejméně tři lidi připravil o život a dalších šest osob zranil ruský útok během noci na úterý na výrobní závod a sklad u města Obuchiv v Kyjevské oblasti, informovali záchranáři z ukrajinské služby pro mimořádné situace (DSNS). Rusové útočili také u obce Čabany a na rozhraní Kyjeva a Kyjevské oblasti. Ukrajinské drony zasáhly ruské Tambovské oblasti zatím blíže neupřesněný podnik.

data.title: Poslanci budou jednat o trestech za týrání zvířat a zákazu lovu norováním
data.description: Poslanci budou v úterý jednat o změně zákona na ochranu zvířat proti týrání. Místo půlročního vězení za to má nově hrozit nejméně roční, uvedl vicepremiér Karel Havlíček. Novela zavede i povinnost obcí zajišťovat na své náklady kastrace opuštěných a zdivočelých koček. Obce by se musely postarat o opuštěné domácí zvíře, které není zdivočelé a o něž nemá nikdo zájem.

Novela zavede i povinnost obcí zajišťovat na své náklady kastrace opuštěných a zdivočelých koček. Obce by se musely postarat o opuštěné domácí zvíře, které není zdivočelé a o něž nemá nikdo zájem.

data.title: Příjmy z prostituce podléhají zdanění, potvrdil Ústavní soud. Stížnost ženy odmítl
data.description: Příjmy z dobrovolně vykonávané prostituce podléhají zdanění stejně jako jiné formy samostatné výdělečné činnosti. Průlomový právní názor Nejvyššího správního soudu ve dvou usneseních potvrdil Ústavní soud, zjistila ČTK ze soudní databáze. Odmítl stížnosti ženy, které úřady zpětně vyměřily daň za roky 2013 a 2014. V obou případech daň činila více než 900 tisíc korun.

data.title: Lampy za miliony, více zeleně. Kampa projde obnovou, otázkou je harmonogram
data.description: Nového veřejného osvětlení se dočká pražský park Kampa. Obnova začíná v úterý, staré lampy nahradí tzv. Pražské lucerny. Jde o součást projektu na celkovou revitalizaci parku u Vltavy, jeho zeleně, chodníků i vybavení. Městská část Praha 1 předpokládá, že práce započnou v prvních měsících roku 2027.

data.title: Na Sicílii se utopila Češka. Pátrali po ní dva dny, její tělo nalezli v přístavu
data.description: V přístavu města Marsala na Sicílii policie a záchranáři v neděli vylovili tělo české turistky, která se utopila. Podle místních médií žena pobývala v přístavu na pronajaté lodi. České ministerstvo zahraničí potvrdilo, že na Sicílii nalezli mrtvou českou občanku. Podle úřadu se po ní pátralo od neděle, kdy její zmizení ohlásili spolucestující z jachty.

data.title: Černý kašel může dál zabíjet. Šancí je také nová vakcína, v Česku zatím není dostupná
data.description: Nečekaně silná epidemie černého kašle, která zasáhla Česko předloni, pomalu odeznívá. Infekce ale dál komplikuje život dětem i dospělým. Letos už onemocnělo okolo tisíce lidí, jeden pacient zemřel. Od roku 2024 si nákaza vyžádala 13 obětí včetně dvou kojenců. Odborníci upozorňují hlavně na riziko pro nejmenší děti a doporučují očkování těhotným ženám. Teď se objevila nová šance, do Evropy míří první monovakcína.

data.title: České lázeňství na křižovatce. Tradice už nestačí, shodují se experti
data.description: Tradiční léčebné pobyty v Česku narážejí na měnící se požadavky klientů, zastaralé provozy i nedostatek personálu. Zatímco Karlovy Vary se po odchodu části ruské klientely přeorientovaly hlavně na Němce, Velichovky třeba polská klientela nezachrání. „Lázně by měly být vnímány jako prevence, ne až jako následná péče,“ říká ředitel Lázní Velichovky Petr Čermák. Spolu s ním byli hosty pořadu iDNES Lounge také Josef Dlohoš, ředitel Infocentra města Karlovy Vary a Jaromír Pažout, spolumajitel a zakladatel Original Beer Spa.

data.title: Rusko Ukrajině nic moc nedělá, chová se přijatelně, prohlásil Trump
data.description: Americký prezident Donald Trump prohlásil, že Rusko toho Ukrajině „moc nedělá“ a chová se „přijatelně“. Ve stejnou dobu ruský úder v parku v Charkovské oblasti zabil šest lidí včetně roční holčičky a další útoky následovaly v noci na úterý. Trump pochválil Rusko i za to, že se drží od Íránu dál. Ukrajinu naopak obvinil, že Američanům nic nedala.

data.title: Volby do Kongresu USA 2026: Midterms mohou Trumpovi vzít kontrolu
data.description: Američany čekají 3. listopadu 2026 důležité volby do Kongresu, známé jako midterms. Nazývají se tak každé volby, které se konají v půlce čtyřletého mandátu prezidenta. Představují totiž zásadní referendum o něm. Pro Donalda Trumpa budou prvním celostátním testem jeho druhého funkčního období. Rozhodne se v nich o složení celé Sněmovny reprezentantů a více než třetině křesel v Senátu.

data.title: Saúdská Arábie ruší kvůli útokům Húsíů letošní „Davos v poušti“
data.description: Saúdská Arábie odložila konání každoroční investiční konference přezdívané Davos v poušti na příští rok. Saúdská Arábie v poslední době čelí vlně útoků jemenských Húsíů.

data.title: Itálie se nabízí jako pokusná země na celoroční zavedení jednoho času
data.description: Osm let čekají miliony Evropanů na to, až se Evropská unie dohodne na ukončení střídání času. Sedmadvacítku členských států zavedla do slepé uličky odpověď na otázku, který čas by měl vlastně platit nastálo. Itálie se z ní rozhodla vykročit a nabízí se jako země, která by vyzkoušela letní čas po celý rok.

data.title: Současné vedení končí. Tábor má koalici, starostou bude Semerák z Našeho Česka
data.description: Uskupení Tábor 2020 nebude mít po 16 letech starostu v druhém největším jihočeském městě. Společně pro Tábor se spojilo s hnutím Naše Česko, ANO a členkou SOCDEM. data.title: CZ IPI se zastalo novinářky Karoliny Brodníčkové, které anonym vyhrožuje smrtí

Politická reportérka deníku Právo a serveru Novinky informuje veřejnost především o české politické scéně a sociálních problémech ve společnosti. Za nepřijatelné, aby se kdokoliv kvůli své práci nebo názorům musel bát o život považuje i prezident Petr Pavel.

data.title: Luxusní zboží z vyrabovaných obchodů ve Francii se objevilo na bazarech

data.title: „Kousl ruku, která ho krmila.“ Kreml si vychutnává roztržku Trumpa a Zelenského
data.description: Kremelští jestřábi si vychutnávají veřejný rozkol mezi americkým prezidentem Donaldem Trumpem a jeho ukrajinským protějškem Volodymyrem Zelenským. data.title: Pacientes con cáncer de mama en Venezuela luchan contra la falta de recursos y el abandono del sistema público
data.description: La escasez de equipos operativos, las dificultades para acceder a medicamentos oncológicos, la concentración de los servicios especializados y el costo de los exámenes retrasan la atención. Bolivia Bocaranda, de SenosAyuda, y Luisa Rodríguez Táriba, de Funcamama, advierten que las organizaciones civiles han tenido que ampliar su labor asistencial ante las fallas del sistema público. Los terremotos de junio sumaron nuevas dificultades para mujeres que perdieron sus viviendas y sus redes de apoyo. The post Pacientes con cáncer de mama en Venezuela luchan contra la falta de recursos y el abandono del sistema público appeared first on EL NACIONAL .

data.title: Interview avec Léonce Ngendakumana : « Le pouvoir actuel est une dictature voilée »
data.description: Le parti Sahwanya-Frodebu a décidé de ne pas présenter un candidat à la présidentielle de 2027. Pour Léonce Ngendakumana, membre de ce parti et ancien président de l’Assemblée nationale, cette décision s’explique par les conditions dans lesquelles le scrutin est organisé. Il dénonce la manipulation du processus électoral et l’impossibilité du pays d’organiser des élections libres et démocratiques. Il revient également sur l’héritage du président Melchior Ndadaye, les divisions au sein du Frodebu et les difficultés économiques du pays.

data.title: Le Cantique de la Primus Ligue – Journées 7 et 8 : Quand le cuir devient serment
data.description: Il est des saisons où le football cesse d'être un simple décompte de points pour se muer en une vaste fresque sentimentale. La Primus Ligue 2026-2027 vit précisément l'une de ces heures enchantées. Aux septième et huitième journées, le Burundi n'a pas seulement compté des buts ; il a vu des destins se nouer, des orgueils se briser et des espérances renaître sous la poussière ocre de ses stades.

data.description: Plusieurs quartiers de la capitale économique burundaise souffrent cruellement de la pénurie d’eau ces derniers jours. Les habitants ne savent plus à quel saint se vouer. data.title: Cameroun : six mois après la saisine de l’UA, Maurice Kamto publie le mémorandum sur le changement anticonstitutionnel de gouvernement
data.description: © (DR) L’universitaire et ancien président du Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun a accusé le gouvernement camerounais d’avoir opéré un changement constitutionnel en violation des dispositions de la Constitution et des textes internationaux. Mais les sanctions demandées à l'UA restent attendues. Le 20 avril 2026, le Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun a saisi le président de la Commission de l’Union africaine S.E Mahmoud Ali Youssouf. Le parti politique camerounais, par l’entremise de son ancien président Maurice Kamto, accusait alors le gouvernement camerounais d’avoir opéré un changement illégal de Constitution. Et de reporter de manière successive et illégale des élections. D’après le mémorandum daté du 20 avril et rendu public le 19 octobre, le MRC expose les faits de la cause. Le gouvernement camerounais a convoqué le Congrès, lequel a modifié certains articles de la Constitution en instaurant un poste de vice-président qui sera pourvu par nomination. Et dont le titulaire sera le successeur du président de la République. Cette démarche est en violation de l’article 64 de la Constitution en vigueur au Cameroun. Il stipule que « aucune procédure de révision ne peut être retenue si elle porte atteinte à la forme républicaine, à l’unité et à l’intégrité territoriale de l’Etat et aux principes démocratiques qui régissent la République ». Or d’après le parti, elle porte atteinte au principe démocratique de l’élection. Elle va aussi à l’encontre des instruments juridiques fondamentaux de l’Union africaine. En l’occurrence le principe de « promouvoir les principes et les institutions démocratiques, la participation populaire et la bonne gouvernance ». Le parti politique soutient aussi que la violation de l’article 64 de la Constitution camerounaise est une violation de l’article 3 paragraphe 10 de la Charte africaine de la démocratie et de la gouvernance et de l’article 4(p) de l’Acte constitutif de l’Union africaine qui rejette et condamne les changements anticonstitutionnels de gouvernements. A propos du report successif des élections, le MRC accuse le gouvernement camerounais d’avoir violé l’article 15(4) de la Constitution camerounaise en reportant les élections législatives ; l’article 3(4) de la Charte africaine de la démocratie et de la gouvernance en reportant les élections municipales ; l’article 25 du pacte international relatif aux droits civils et politiques pour les deux types d’élections. Les prorogations de mandats des députés et conseillers municipaux 2025-2026 et 2026-2027 privent les populations de l’exercice de leur droit de vote et portent ainsi atteinte aux principes démocratiques, relève le parti d’opposition. Au regard de ces différents faits, le MRC formule ses prétentions auprès de l’Union africaine. Le parti demande à l’organisation de sanctionner le Cameroun en appliquant des mesures prévues dans des textes. Il s’agit en l’occurrence de la suspension de la participation de l’Etat du Cameroun à l’Union africaine ; des actions diplomatiques en vue du rétablissement des mécanismes constitutionnels de dévolution démocratiques du pouvoir par les élections ; l’engagement à respecter la Constitution et l’Etat de droit et la garantie de non-répétition des actes de changement anticonstitutionnel de gouvernement. Le Parti demande par ailleurs d’interdire les voyages, de refuser la délivrance de visas, de geler les avoirs à l’encontre des auteurs de changement anticonstitutionnel de gouvernement ; sans oublier les restrictions commerciales. Mais, six mois après la saisine de l’Union africaine et le dépôt du mémorandum, le parti d’opposition ne présente pas de réponse de l’organisation continentale. Au pays, l’Etat continue de fonctionner avec les mêmes institutions et les changements décriés par le MRC. Alors que ce parti dénonce un coup d’Etat constitutionnel, d’autres partis malgré tout, demandent au chef de l’Etat de nommer le vice-président. Cet article Cameroun : six mois après la saisine de l’UA, Maurice Kamto publie le mémorandum sur le changement anticonstitutionnel de gouvernement est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Emplois verts : le Minefop vise 12 0000 emplois d’ici 2029
data.description: © DR Placée sous le thème « Entrepreneuriat vert et transition écologique », la 2e édition des emplois verts s'est ouverte lundi 19 octobre 2026 à Yaoundé. Le vert comme gisement d'emplois. Le Ministre de l'Emploi et de la Formation Professionnelle a ouvert officiellement, le lundi 19 octobre 2026 au Majestic Cinéma à Yaoundé, la 2e édition de la Semaine des emplois verts. Organisée du 16 au 20 octobre 2026 par le MINEFOP à travers le Programme de Promotion des Emplois Verts au Cameroun (PPEVC), l'initiative fait suite à la première édition de mai 2024. Elle vise à promouvoir la création d'emplois verts durables par l'entrepreneuriat. Pour la période 2025-2029, le PPEVC ambitionne de créer ou verdir 120 000 emplois décents. Il s'appuie sur 11 projets pilotes – solaire de proximité, recyclage des déchets, aquaculture, reboisement, BTP vert – et une stratégie de financement de plus de 21,15 milliards FCFA. Six filières porteuses ont été identifiées : énergie solaire, recyclage plastique, agriculture biologique et cacao, construction en terre stabilisée, écotourisme et numérique vert. Dans son discours, le Ministre a affirmé qu'« il ne peut y avoir d'emplois verts durables sans compétences adaptées ». Il a rappelé que 5 000 des 25 000 bourses gratuites de l'opération ORFEV-JEUNES concernent les métiers verts et annoncé le lancement des formations 2026/2027 de l'initiative JEME (un jeune, un métier, un emploi). Face aux inondations, à la désertification et à la déforestation, il a appelé à transformer les contraintes climatiques en opportunités, invitant les jeunes à entreprendre et les entreprises à investir dans les compétences vertes. Cet article Emplois verts : le Minefop vise 12 0000 emplois d’ici 2029 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: CITS : ONU Femmes mise sur le numérique pour l’avenir des filles au Cameroun
data.description: © DR Du 15 au 17 octobre 2026 au Palais des Congrès de Yaoundé, ONU Femmes Cameroun a pris part au Cameroon International Tech Summit pour promouvoir une transformation numérique inclusive au service des droits des filles. Le numérique comme levier d'émancipation. C'est le message porté par ONU Femmes Cameroun au Cameroon International Tech Summit 2026. Du 15 au 17 octobre 2026, au Palais des Congrès de Yaoundé, l'agence onusienne a pris part au CITS 2026 à travers le Stand One UN. Une participation qui a permis de promouvoir une transformation numérique inclusive, porteuse d'opportunités pour les femmes et les jeunes. Le sommet a réuni les acteurs de l'écosystème autour de thématiques majeures : compétences numériques, emploi des jeunes, startups, intelligence artificielle, fintech et innovation. Temps fort de cette présence, à l'occasion de la Journée internationale de la fille, ONU Femmes Cameroun et X Code Path ont animé une session sur le thème : « Mon avenir, mon choix : les compétences technologiques au service des droits des filles ». Le constat est sans appel : les compétences numériques sont de puissants leviers pour renforcer l'autonomisation et l'inclusion des filles et des jeunes femmes, tout en élargissant leur accès aux opportunités. En facilitant l'accès à l'information, à l'apprentissage, à l'innovation et aux perspectives économiques, les compétences numériques et technologiques contribuent directement à l'autonomisation des filles. ONU Femmes réaffirme ainsi son engagement en faveur d'un numérique accessible et inclusif, afin que chaque fille puisse apprendre, innover et construire librement son avenir. Cet article CITS : ONU Femmes mise sur le numérique pour l’avenir des filles au Cameroun est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun/ Droit des filles : un atelier pour un agenda national
data.description: © DR Du 19 au 23 octobre 2026, Douala abrite l'atelier du Groupe de travail multisectoriel chargé d'élaborer l'Agenda national pour les droits des filles. Cap sur des engagements concrets pour les filles au Cameroun. Du 19 au 23 octobre 2026, Douala accueille l'atelier du Groupe de travail multisectoriel pour l'élaboration de l'Agenda national pour les droits des filles au Cameroun. La cérémonie d'ouverture a été présidée par M. Nguélé Elie Bertrand, Directeur de la Promotion et de la Protection de la Famille et des Droits de l'Enfant, aux côtés du Dr Patricia Norolalao, Spécialiste du développement des adolescents et du genre à l'UNICEF Cameroun. Un duo État-partenaire technique qui donne le ton de cette rencontre. L'objectif est clair : consolider les six priorités et les 24 engagements déjà proposés, définir des actions concrètes, mobiliser les ressources nécessaires et établir des mécanismes efficaces de suivi et de redevabilité. Il ne s'agit plus seulement d'énoncer des principes, mais de les traduire en actes. Le changement attendu est de taille : doter le Cameroun d'un Agenda national opérationnel, assorti d'engagements mesurables, pour renforcer la protection des droits des filles et favoriser leur participation effective à la vie sociale et politique. Parce que chaque fille mérite de voir ses droits respectés, protégés et pleinement réalisés, l'atelier de Douala se veut le point de départ d'une nouvelle dynamique politique en faveur de l'égalité. Cet article Cameroun/ Droit des filles : un atelier pour un agenda national est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Particularités de l’interface 1XBET et méthodes de navigation dans les principales sections
data.description: © 1xbet L’interface 1XBET regroupe plusieurs rubriques consacrées aux paris sportifs et aux divertissements en ligne. Son organisation permet aux utilisateurs de consulter les compétitions, de rechercher des rencontres et d’accéder aux différentes fonctionnalités. Les menus principaux facilitent le passage d’une section à une autre. Les catégories sportives occupent une place importante dans la navigation. Quelques repères suffisent pour comprendre la structure générale du site et retrouver les informations recherchées. Les éléments principaux de l’interface La page d’accueil présente généralement les rubriques essentielles et les événements sportifs disponibles. Le menu principal sert de point de départ pour accéder aux différentes catégories. Les compétitions peuvent être classées par sport, pays ou championnat. Des filtres permettent de réduire la liste affichée et de retrouver plus facilement une rencontre précise. Cette organisation aide les visiteurs à consulter les informations sans parcourir toutes les pages. Pour prendre ses repères, il est utile de procéder par étapes : Repérer le menu principal et les catégories proposées. Choisir un sport ou une compétition pour afficher les événements correspondants. Navigation dans les sections sportives Les rubriques sportives permettent de consulter les matchs de football, les rencontres de basketball, les tournois de tennis et d’autres disciplines. Chaque catégorie rassemble les événements associés, avec des informations comme les équipes participantes, les horaires et les cotes disponibles. Pour mieux connaître les particularités des paris sur le football, les lecteurs peuvent consulter les informations présentées sur https://foot-africa.com/paris-sportifs/1xbet/ . La présentation peut varier selon le sport sélectionné. Les rencontres en direct disposent généralement d’une rubrique spécifique. Il reste important de vérifier les horaires et les données affichées avant toute décision. Voici quelques éléments que les utilisateurs peuvent retrouver : Football : championnats nationaux, coupes et compétitions internationales. Basketball et tennis : matchs, tournois et informations associées. Les fonctionnalités et leurs emplacements Les sections complémentaires donnent accès au compte personnel, à l’historique des opérations et aux paramètres disponibles. Leur emplacement dépend de la version du site et de l’appareil utilisé. Le tableau suivant résume les fonctions courantes et leur utilité. Section Fonction principale Accueil Présentation des rubriques et événements Sports Recherche de compétitions Direct Consultation des matchs en cours Compte Gestion du profil personnel Historique Consultation des opérations précédentes Utilisation sur ordinateur et téléphone Sur ordinateur, l’écran plus large permet souvent d’afficher plusieurs informations simultanément. Sur téléphone, les menus peuvent être adaptés à une présentation verticale et compacte. Les icônes servent alors de raccourcis vers les principales rubriques. Une connexion stable facilite le chargement des pages et l’actualisation des données. Les fonctionnalités accessibles peuvent aussi varier selon le pays et les règles locales. Cet article Particularités de l’interface 1XBET et méthodes de navigation dans les principales sections est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
