data.title: La CSJ enviará su opinión sobre reformas penales este martes, afirma Wagner Vallecillo
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- El presidente de la Corte Suprema de Justicia (CSJ), Wagner Vallecillo , informó que el pleno de magistrados remitirá este martes 20 de octubre al Congreso Nacional su opinión sobre las propuestas de reformas al Código Penal y al Código Procesal Penal . Vallecillo explicó que convocó a una sesión del pleno para conocer los criterios de la Sala de lo Penal sobre las dos propuestas de reforma y prevé que el documento sea enviado al Legislativo antes de las 5:00 p. m. , para que los diputados puedan considerarla durante la discusión. Asimismo, el titular del Poder Judicial aclaró que el pronunciamiento de la Corte Suprema de Justicia tendrá carácter ilustrativo y no será vinculante para los diputados, quienes tendrán la facultad de decidir cuáles de las recomendaciones incorporan a las reformas. "Nosotros solo aplicamos la ley y quien reforma las leyes es el Congreso Nacional de la República, ellos toman sus decisiones de cuáles adoptan y cuáles no adoptan”, manifestó Vallecillo. Por otra parte, Vallecillo se refirió a la posibilidad de reducir la edad punible en Honduras y aseguró que el tema no ha sido abordado por el pleno de magistrados, por lo que expresó dudas de que sea discutido en esta ocasión. El presidente de la CSJ recordó que el país es parte de tratados y convenios internacionales, por lo que destacó que debe prevalecer el interés superior del menor al analizar cualquier medida relacionada con la responsabilidad penal de niños y adolescentes. En otro tema, Vallecillo anunció que el Poder Judicial solicitó un incremento presupuestario para instalar y fortalecer los circuitos especiales, una petición que fue planteada ante el Congreso Nacional después de realizar el trámite correspondiente con la Secretaría de Finanzas. La solicitud se enmarca en los esfuerzos de coordinación entre el Poder Judicial, el Ministerio Público y las secretarías de Seguridad y Defensa para mejorar la investigación y el procesamiento de los delitos en el país. Finalmente, el funcionario informó que la institución prevé abrir un concurso para cubrir las plazas disponibles y realizar una evaluación general de sus servidores, cuyos resultados podrían derivar en medidas de depuración dentro del sistema judicial. El pasado 12 de octubre, el Congreso Nacional impulsó reformas al Código Penal y al Código Procesal Penal orientadas a endurecer las medidas contra las pandillas, la delincuencia y el crimen organizado. Entre las propuestas figuran la posibilidad de efectuar allanamientos sin orden judicial previa en determinadas circunstancias, ampliar de 24 a 48 horas el plazo para presentar requerimientos fiscales después de una captura y restringir el acceso a la libertad condicional y a mecanismos de preliberación para personas condenadas por terrorismo. Tomás Zambrano, presentó esta disposición como parte de un endurecimiento de las consecuencias penales para los integrantes de las estructuras declaradas terroristas. “Estas son medidas históricas. Desde el Congreso no vamos a descansar hasta que Honduras pueda vivir nuevamente en paz y tranquilidad, y que la gente salga segura de sus casas con su familia, como lo hacía en los años 80 y 90, sin miedo ni temor”, sentenció.

El presidente de la CSJ recordó que el país es parte de tratados y convenios internacionales, por lo que destacó que debe prevalecer el interés superior del menor al analizar cualquier medida relacionada con la responsabilidad penal de niños y adolescentes. En otro tema, Vallecillo anunció que el Poder Judicial solicitó un incremento presupuestario para instalar y fortalecer los circuitos especiales, una petición que fue planteada ante el Congreso Nacional después de realizar el trámite correspondiente con la Secretaría de Finanzas. La solicitud se enmarca en los esfuerzos de coordinación entre el Poder Judicial, el Ministerio Público y las secretarías de Seguridad y Defensa para mejorar la investigación y el procesamiento de los delitos en el país. Finalmente, el funcionario informó que la institución prevé abrir un concurso para cubrir las plazas disponibles y realizar una evaluación general de sus servidores, cuyos resultados podrían derivar en medidas de depuración dentro del sistema judicial. El pasado 12 de octubre, el Congreso Nacional impulsó reformas al Código Penal y al Código Procesal Penal orientadas a endurecer las medidas contra las pandillas, la delincuencia y el crimen organizado. Entre las propuestas figuran la posibilidad de efectuar allanamientos sin orden judicial previa en determinadas circunstancias, ampliar de 24 a 48 horas el plazo para presentar requerimientos fiscales después de una captura y restringir el acceso a la libertad condicional y a mecanismos de preliberación para personas condenadas por terrorismo. Tomás Zambrano, presentó esta disposición como parte de un endurecimiento de las consecuencias penales para los integrantes de las estructuras declaradas terroristas. “Estas son medidas históricas. Desde el Congreso no vamos a descansar hasta que Honduras pueda vivir nuevamente en paz y tranquilidad, y que la gente salga segura de sus casas con su familia, como lo hacía en los años 80 y 90, sin miedo ni temor”, sentenció.

data.title: Paralizada desde hace 67 días la pavimentación de carretera a Lepaterique
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- La pavimentación de la carretera que conduce a Lepaterique, Francisco Morazán, permanece paralizada desde hace 67 días, luego de que la maquinaria y los trabajadores de la Secretaría de Infraestructura y Transporte (SIT) dejaran de laborar en el proyecto, que apenas registra dos kilómetros de avance desde el inicio de los trabajos de campo . El proyecto vial tiene retrasos a pese al compromiso del gobierno de construir una carretera de concreto hidráulico para mejorar la conexión entre Lepaterique y la capital hondureña. La promesa de pavimentación se anunció desde el 10 de abril de 2024, cuando los pobladores realizaron una toma de carretera para exigir una ruta vial digna. En aquel momento, la inversión anunciada rondaba los 35 millones de dólares; sin embargo, los compromisos iniciales no se tradujeron en el comienzo oportuno de las obras y los habitantes continuaron a la espera de una respuesta concreta para mejorar las condiciones de la carretera. La contratación formal llegó posteriormente y el 15 de marzo de 2025 se suscribió el contrato SIT-CO-109-2025 para pavimentar aproximadamente cinco kilómetros del tramo de Lepaterique hacia aldea Mateo, por un monto inicial de 65,511,945.11 lempiras. El contrato establecía un plazo de ejecución de 210 días calendario a partir de la orden de inicio, que fue emitida el 7 de julio de 2025. Para mayo de 2026, el proyecto comenzó a ejecutarse ; sin embargo, cinco meses después, los trabajos quedaron abandonados con apenas dos kilómetros de pavimento de concreto hidráulico. Para los habitantes, la pavimentación representa una oportunidad para mejorar la movilidad y facilitar el traslado de productos y facilitar el transporte en vehículos y motocicletas. Durante años, los pobladores han denunciado las dificultades que enfrentan para circular por la carretera, especialmente durante el invierno, cuando las condiciones del terreno complican el tránsito. En verano, el polvo también afecta a quienes viven y trabajan a lo largo del recorrido.

data.title: „Dronatonas“ finišavo surinkęs 1,3 mln. eurų: jau perkami dronai-perėmėjai
data.description: Aštuonias savaites trukusi „Blue/Yellow“ paramos kampanija „Dronatonas“ baigėsi surinkus 1 301 494 eurus. Šiemet kampanijos lėšos skirtos abiejų šalių oro gynybai: 80 proc. sumos tenka Ukrainos pajėgoms, o 20 proc. – Lietuvos šaulių sąjungai (LŠS). Už šias lėšas perkami dronai-perėmėjai, antidroninės sistemos bei finansuojami operatorių mokymai, rašoma „Blue/Yellow“ pranešime žiniasklaidai.

data.title: Damen challenges Rheinmetall’s EUR 138 mln acquisition of Mangalia shipyard in Romania
data.description: The Dutch company Damen Holding BV, the previous operator of the ailing Mangalia shipyard in Romania, has challenged in court the tender through which German defense manufacturer Rheinmetall won the auction for the shipyard on October 9, 2026, offering EUR 138 million. Damen is the main creditor of the Mangalia Shipyard. The company challenged the court ruling that allowed the starting price to be reduced as part of the shipyard's sale procedure, paving the way for its acquisition by Rheinmetall earlier this month, after four unsuccessful attempts. The sale price of EUR 138 million is equivalent to 75% of the initial starting price of EUR 184 million. The court's decision to allow the starting price to be reduced was justified by the lack of bidders in the first four tenders held. Judicial liquidator CITR asked the insolvency judge on May 14, 2026, to approve the application of the provisions of the Civil Procedure Code, which allowed the price to be reduced to 75% of its initial value. A few hours later, Damen Holding BV filed a request proposing a different strategy: holding six consecutive monthly tenders without reducing the starting price. However, the Creditors' Meeting, in which Damen Holding holds 70% of the total claims, approved the strategy proposed by the liquidator. After the first three tenders held under this strategy attracted no buyers, the insolvency judge subsequently allowed the price to be reduced in accordance with the Civil Procedure Code, and Rheinmetall won the fifth tender. In the challenge it filed, Damen Holding argued that applying the legal provisions concerning the price reduction is erroneous in light of recent legislative amendments. “The law no longer refers to the maximum 12-month period for the sale of assets, and the notion of a ‘reasonable period’ remains undefined,” the document consulted by News.ro stated . Meanwhile, representatives of the 2 May naval shipyard, which is controlled by the Romanian state and is the majority shareholder in Damen Mangalia, with a 51% stake, accused Damen Holding of obstructing the sale process. They claimed that the Dutch company was allowed to attend Creditors' Meeting sessions to approve the proposed sale strategy, but was absent or opposed it, thereby contributing to delays in the process. They also stressed that the accumulation of current debts during the bankruptcy period reduces the chances of recovering claims. The case will be examined by the Constanța Tribunal on November 4. Rheinmetall announced on Monday, October 19, that it intends to develop a “dual-use” production center at Mangalia, for both military and civilian purposes, in partnership with Swiss shipping company MSC. “Following the acquisition, we plan to expand and upgrade the shipyard comprehensively. We aim to further develop the existing infrastructure, improve production conditions and adapt capacity to meet future requirements. This will enable the site in the long term to play a key role in the implementation of our strategic activities in South-Eastern Europe and to strengthen our industrial presence in the region,” said Tim Wagner, CEO of the Naval Systems division.

We aim to further develop the existing infrastructure, improve production conditions and adapt capacity to meet future requirements. This will enable the site in the long term to play a key role in the implementation of our strategic activities in South-Eastern Europe and to strengthen our industrial presence in the region,” said Tim Wagner, CEO of the Naval Systems division.

data.title: MerchantPro Compass: First Quarter of Dual Taxation on Non-EU Parcels Brings 13% More Orders to Local Online Stores. Fashion Rebounds from Stagnation to 17% Growth
data.description: After a first half of the year in which market growth was driven almost entirely by higher basket values, Romanian eCommerce shifted direction in the third quarter, the first in which parcels arriving from outside the European Union were subject to both national and EU-level taxes. The MerchantPro Compass analysis, conducted by MerchantPro, a SaaS eCommerce solutions platform supporting more than 2,000 active online stores, is based on a representative sample of stores operating on the platform during both periods under comparison. The data shows that, for the first time in nearly two years, market growth is being driven by order volumes rather than basket values, as local online retailers begin to regain ground in the categories most exposed to international competition. In the first nine months of 2026, sales value increased by 8.5% compared with the same period last year, while order volumes rose by nearly 6%. The average order value reached €59, up 2.5%. Much of this growth was driven by the third quarter, when order volumes increased by 12.6%, virtually matching the 12% rise in sales value, while the average basket remained stable at €60. By comparison, order volumes had grown by only approximately 2.5% during the first two quarters. Where the first effects of taxes on non-EU parcels are becoming visible The RON 25 logistics tax, introduced in January for parcels valued below €150 arriving from outside the European Union, was supplemented on July 1 by an EU customs duty of €3 for each product category contained in a parcel. Combined, the two charges can add nearly 40% to the cost of a €20 order, enough to erode the price advantage that Asian platforms have built, particularly in the low-value purchase segment. Although the impact of these taxes cannot be fully isolated from other factors influencing consumer spending, performance across sectors suggests that some demand has begun shifting back toward local online retailers. The strongest third-quarter results were recorded precisely in the categories most exposed to international competition: Fashion, the sector with the highest number of orders, moved from flat performance in the first half of the year to 17% growth in order volumes and 13% growth in sales value in Q3. Average order value declined by 3%, indicating a return of lower-value purchases. Children's Products narrowed the decline in order volumes from 18% in the first half of the year to less than 5% in Q3, with sales value virtually unchanged from last year. Automotive & Motorcycle Products and Sporting Goods both recorded 16% growth in order volumes in Q3, accompanied by declining average order values. "For the first time in nearly two years, growth is coming from order volumes rather than higher basket values. The number of orders increased at the same pace as sales, with growth concentrated in lower-value purchases, precisely the segment that non-EU platforms have dominated in recent years. The recovery is taking place in the categories where competition from these platforms has been fiercest, including fashion, toys and accessories, and coincides with the point at which parcel taxes began to affect final prices. > > I don't believe taxes alone explain this development. Inflation fell to 6.2% in August, from more than 10% in June, while the third quarter of last year was particularly weak, affected by the VAT increase and rising energy prices. However, the taxes have narrowed a price gap that was difficult for local retailers to overcome, especially on small orders." says Arthur Radulescu, CEO of MerchantPro. Sector performance ranges from +37% to -15% Electronics, Gadgets & Accessories remains the fastest-growing sector, with sales value up 37% and order volumes up 33% in the first nine months of the year. This momentum continued into the third quarter, with sales value rising 37% and order volumes increasing 38%, while the average basket remained stable at €90. Meanwhile, Home & Deco , one of the largest sectors by sales value, accelerated in the third quarter, recording 14% growth in sales value and 10% growth in orders, following a first half in which order volumes had stagnated. At the opposite end of the spectrum, Beauty remains the only major sector to record a decline over the nine-month period, with both sales value and order volumes down 15%. Average order value remained unchanged at approximately €42, indicating that the decline was driven by fewer orders rather than consumers switching to lower-priced products. Over the same period, Pharma recorded 23% growth in sales value and a one-third increase in order volumes. In the third quarter, Pharma's growth rate moderated to 15%, while Beauty's decline narrowed from 19% in the first half of the year to 7%. "Beauty and Pharma are increasingly overlapping, particularly in dermocosmetics, which online pharmacies offer at comparable prices alongside products consumers already purchase regularly. Most likely, some of the demand lost by Beauty has shifted to pharmacies. The fact that Beauty's decline narrowed in the third quarter while Pharma's growth moderated leads us to believe that this shift in demand is beginning to stabilize." explains Arthur Radulescu, CEO of MerchantPro. Books & Music (+11% in sales value over nine months) is growing almost exclusively through higher average order values, while Jewelry (+10%) is also driven primarily by this factor. Food Products (+10% in sales value and +15% in order volumes), meanwhile, follows the opposite pattern. At the same time, the B2B sector recorded the fastest growth in order volumes among the major categories in the sample, with one-third more orders in the first nine months and a 41% increase in the third quarter. This represents a growth rate four times higher than that of sales value, confirming the trend identified at mid-year. Online commerce grows as physical retail declines The performance of online commerce contrasts with that of the overall retail sector. According to Romania's National Institute of Statistics (INS), retail turnover volume declined by 5% in the first eight months of 2026, with August marking the first month of the year to record slightly positive growth. Over the same period, order volumes in MerchantPro's sample increased by nearly 6%, suggesting that a growing share of consumer spending is shifting online, even in a year marked by cautious spending. "For merchants, the challenge now is to make sure they can be found by returning shoppers. A tax can increase the cost of an order, but it does not change where the purchasing journey begins, and today that journey increasingly starts on a marketplace or through an AI assistant. The most important commercial period of the year is approaching, with Black Friday and the holiday shopping season, while the European handling fee for non-EU parcels is also expected to come into force in the coming period. From 2028, the customs reform will completely eliminate the special regime for low-value parcels. The price gap with international platforms will narrow, but it will not disappear, meaning competitive advantage can no longer be built on price alone. Merchants who use the coming months to better understand their customers through data, personalization and frictionless shopping experiences will be able to turn a temporary recovery into long-term customer relationships." says Arthur Radulescu. According to the MerchantPro eCommerce Insights 2026 report, which combines proprietary platform data with public sources and macroeconomic indicators, Romania's eCommerce market exceeded €8.1 billion in 2025 and is expected to surpass €8.5 billion in 2026, with an estimated growth rate of approximately 5%. Results for the first nine months are consistent with this forecast, while third-quarter performance suggests that growth could even exceed expectations if the momentum continues through the year-end shopping season.

data.title: Romanian electronics retailer Flanco launches Black Friday discounts
data.description: Flanco, a major electronics retailer in Romania, announced the 16th edition of Black Friday, running from October 22 to November 30, in more than 150 stores nationwide and online. “Over the almost six-week campaign, we will add new products to the offer in three stages, so that customers can always find available stock, new discounts, and relevant options for different needs and budgets,” promised Dragoș Sîrbu, Flanco CEO. Among the items up for sale are electronics and IT products, with discounts of up to 41% on TVs, up to 50% on IT products, up to 54% on small household appliances, and up to 41% on headphones and phones. Discounts on large household appliances reach up to RON 1,500, while those on smartphones reach up to RON 1,000. The company also announced that customers can opt to purchase any product with 24 interest-free installments. The offer of 24 interest-free installments on any product remains available during Black Friday, giving customers the option to spread the purchase cost over a period of two years. In addition, all other financing solutions and the retailer’s Rabla programs will remain active throughout the campaign. Through the Rabla programs, customers can recycle used equipment and receive vouchers worth up to RON 300 toward the purchase of small and large household appliances, automatic espresso machines, laptops, and TVs. For smartphones, the program offers an instant discount of up to 30% on the purchase of a new phone in exchange for an old one. Customers will also continue to benefit from the extended 45-day free return period and various delivery options, including courier delivery, collection from more than 7,000 lockers, or pickup from the network’s 150 stores.

data.title: Outgoing PM Ilie Bolojan warns Romania could derail again if next government abandons reforms
data.description: Ilie Bolojan, who was appointed prime minister of Romania in June 2025 and became the longest-serving interim PM since his dismissal in May of this year, took stock of his mandate at the helm of the executive on Monday, October 19, in a press conference. Fiscal measures Bolojan, who is also president of the National Liberal Party (PNL), has continuously battled a ballooning public deficit throughout his mandate, with moderate success. This week, the government announced that the general government budget deficit contracted by 23% y/y to RON 78.5 billion (EUR 14.7 billion) in January-September 2026, accounting for 3.8% of GDP, down from 5.3% of GDP in the same period of 2025. Bolojan took credit for the lower deficit during the conference, and said that when he took office, the country had its “back against the wall,” but that he had managed to avoid a downgrade and begin a series of reforms. “We were forced to start by increasing VAT. We urgently needed to bring money into the budget and reduce the deficit. We did not hide anything from Romanians, we did not change the figures, and we refused to make promises without backing,” Ilie Bolojan said. The interim PM thanked employees, entrepreneurs, and pensioners for the financial strains they had to bear in the past year, particularly higher living costs and taxation. He also spoke about the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR). “I found it blocked, overcontracted, delayed, and on the verge of failure. We renegotiated it and restarted it. Romania has so far received 65% of the value of the PNRR and still has two payment requests pending review by the European Commission. These would bring the total to 90% of the grant initially allocated. The percentage would have been close to 100% if the PSD (the Social Democratic Party) had not blocked the adoption of the unified pay law in August,” he said. Ilie Bolojan underlined that despite the deficit, investments had increased by more than RON 25 billion compared with the same period last year, from RON 82 billion to RON 107 billion, with more than two-thirds of this amount represented by payments through European projects. Similarly, in the first eight months of 2026, personnel expenses totaled RON 122 billion, RON 4.3 billion less than in the same period last year. “We are leaving the budget on a sound trajectory, and the next government must maintain a prudent budgetary approach and strengthen the economic growth model based on investment rather than consumption. We must tell the truth and reject populism. Debts allegedly left behind by this government are being cited during this period. I have not left debts behind, but Romania has structural problems, and I will not avoid mentioning them, because they will be the challenges facing future governments,” Bolojan added. Accusations targeted at PSD During the press conference, Bolojan blamed the Social Democratic Party (PSD), PNL’s former coalition partners, for sabotaging agreed-upon reforms. “Public administration reform was postponed for months, until February this year. (...) If they had not blocked a large part of the reforms, Romania would now be in a much better situation, but the reforms affected powerful interests,” Bolojan stressed. He said he had launched a war against waste, sinecures, and institutions that consume resources. At the same time, he said he respects public officials who serve the state. According to Ilie Bolojan, “the reform of magistrates’ pensions was unprecedented, something no one had dared to take responsibility for.” He also recalled the judgments that had become enforceable following lawsuits brought by magistrates in Romania. “As you know, we have a judgment obliging the government to pay more than RON 5 billion, and there are also other judgments obtained following the thousands of lawsuits brought over all these years. Without legislation that prevents this type of lawsuit, which is what the adoption of the unified pay law in the Senate would achieve, we will not solve this problem and, regardless of what the next government does, it will effectively be impossible to pay such sums overnight,” he said. https://www.facebook.com/guv.ro/videos/2215854809363643 Energy cost Among the issues tackled by the government, Ilie Bolojan said, were those in the energy sector. “We inherited [the costs of] electricity compensation schemes dating back to 2021, which still involve bills that have not been checked by ANRE and which will continue to come in the following years. This year, we allocated RON 3.7 billion to pay these outstanding amounts and have paid approximately RON 1.5 billion. If all checks are completed satisfactorily, the remaining amounts will also be paid by the end of the year,” the interim prime minister said. Costs accrued as part of these schemes will continue to weigh heavily on the state budget, he warned. Healthcare issues Bolojan stressed that another category of structural problems concerned the healthcare sector. “6.5 million Romanians paid health contributions while 16.5 million benefited from services. This system could not function. Following the measures adopted, 10.5 million Romanians are now contributing, and for the first time, this year the system is approaching a certain balance. However, without measures to incorporate the impact of healthcare salary costs, which lead to poor management in a large proportion of hospitals, into the cost of services provided by hospitals to patients, nothing has been done, and healthcare problems will persist in the coming years,” he said. Public investments According to Bolojan, there is also a major structural problem with investment management. “One of the mistakes made over all these years was overcontracting investments. We still have substantial overcontracting under the Transport Sectoral Program, exceeding 300%. The same situation exists under the program expanding water and sewerage networks. If proper management is not implemented to prioritize investments and retain viable projects across the country, problems will arise regarding payments in the construction sector, the pace of works, and rising costs that the state budget will have to bear,” he said. To make his case, Bolojan pointed to the Transport Ministry, which had been run by the Social Democratic ministers until the dismissal of the government. The institution racked up contracts worth more than EUR 30 billion, while the average annual budget is approximately EUR 6 billion, according to the outgoing PM. “This means we have at least five years of work ahead. Therefore, every project that is launched must be carefully planned to ensure that funding can be secured; otherwise, things will not work out,” Bolojan said. Bolojan also said that, regarding payments to local authorities, the outstanding invoices under the Anghel Saligny program, amounting to RON 2.4 billion, could be paid without difficulty because a budget adjustment was needed. “Furthermore, by releasing the 10% holdback imposed at the beginning of each year through the budget adjustment, all construction invoices due for payment can be settled without difficulty, including those issued by the end of the year,” Ilie Bolojan explained. State-owned companies The prime minister said that the final structural problem that Romania faced concerned the management of state-owned companies. “At the end of every year, companies that have not undergone any reforms for years and need restructuring and intervention always ask for additional subsidy funds in November and December because they fail to prepare their budgets properly. CFR, Metrorex, and so on. Without proper management of state-owned companies, without changing performance indicators and introducing new management contracts, we will not be able to ensure that important state assets are managed better in the interests of citizens,” Ilie Bolojan said. He added that he had begun addressing these imbalances, which had accumulated over previous years, and had managed to correct them partially, whereas previous governments had avoided these problems instead of solving them. “Since taking office, my only concern has been Romania. I do not claim to have been without fault, nor that some things could not have been done better. Perhaps some things escaped our attention, but I leave with the feeling that I have done my duty to our country. If the next government ignores the recent lessons and returns to old, unhealthy habits, it will only be a matter of time before Romania goes off the rails again,” Ilie Bolojan said in his statement delivered at Victoria Palace.

data.title: AI-generated bear image triggers RO-Alert warning in Romanian city
data.description: An AI-generated image purporting to show a bear on a street in Câmpina, Prahova county, prompted a 112 emergency call and a citywide RO-Alert warning. However, the gendarmes dispatched to the area found no witnesses who had actually seen the animal, according to Agerpres . The incident occurred on October 18, when a caller reported the suspected presence of a bear on a street in the city. The caller showed officers a photograph received through WhatsApp that appeared to place the animal in the area. “Those contacted said they had also received the photograph from other people, without being able to identify a genuine source confirming the animal’s presence,” Câmpina City Hall said . The investigators concluded that the image had been created using artificial intelligence and repeatedly forwarded between users. No evidence confirming that a bear had entered the city was found. The City Hall urged residents to verify alarming material before sharing it on social media or messaging services. “Images generated or altered using artificial intelligence can be very difficult to distinguish from genuine ones and may lead to the spread of false information, creating unjustified panic,” the municipality said. The authorities nevertheless advised residents to call 112 when there are genuine indications that a bear or another wild animal is present, providing precise information about the location and circumstances of the sighting. Bears were previously spotted in Câmpina.

data.title: EIB Group and BCR Social Finance expand funding for Romanian microbusinesses
data.description: The EIB announced that it will lend EUR 50 million to BCR Social Finance, which will provide an equal amount from its own resources and distribute the total to microenterprises across Romania. The package will offer lower interest rates than would otherwise be available without EIB involvement. “Europe’s investment ambitions must reach every part of the economy, including its smallest businesses,” EIB vice president Ioannis Tsakiris said. “This loan [...] gives entrepreneurs across Romania greater access to the long-term finance they need to invest, adapt, and grow.” Microenterprises are defined as companies with fewer than 10 employees and annual revenue or a balance-sheet total of no more than EUR 2 million. A separate agreement backed by an InvestEU guarantee from the European Investment Fund will make EUR 100 million available to more than 5,300 Romanian microentrepreneurs, particularly in rural areas. An additional EUR 10 million will support investments in education and skills development. “For a microbusiness, access to the right financing at the right time can make the difference between an investment that happens and one that is postponed,” said BCR Social Finance CEO Ștefan Ionuț Buciuc. BCR Social Finance is a non-bank financial institution owned by Erste Social Finance Holding and Banca Comercială Română. It provides financing to small businesses, social enterprises, students and nongovernmental organizations that may have difficulty accessing traditional bank loans.

data.title: Romanian director Bogdan Mureșanu’s animated short The Magician makes Oscars longlist
data.description: Romanian director Bogdan Mureșanu’s animated short The Magician has joined the pool of films eligible for consideration at the 99th Academy Awards. The film was named best animated short at Romania’s 2026 Gopo Awards. The production premiered internationally at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival in 2025 and recently screened at the Dallas International Film Festival. It also received a special mention at the Bucharest Short Film Festival. Its festival run has included several Oscar-qualifying events, including Spain’s Huesca International Film Festival, HollyShorts and RiverRun in the United States, Ireland’s Dingle Animation Film Festival, and the Tirana International Film Festival. “The fact that, six years later, history is repeating itself in such a beautiful and surprising way, with a place on the longlist for the Oscar nominations, makes me happy and honored,” Bogdan Mureșanu said. He thanked international distributor Mailuki Films, the production team and those who supported the project. Based on a story published in Mureșanu’s short-fiction collection Errata , the film is set in Sulina in 1910, on the evening the Danube port inaugurates its first power plant. Its protagonist, the magician Ilarion, is caught in a forbidden love story while worrying about how he will earn a living in an increasingly modern world. “I had long wanted to bring a vanished world back to life, and animation allowed me to recreate the settings in which the story unfolds from still images,” director Mureșanu said. “Animation was a medium that suited my intention: not to illustrate the glory of a lost world, but to represent the essence of the story.” The voice cast includes Cosmin Șofron, Mihai Gruia Sandu, Ioana Flora, Olimpia Melinte, Valeriu Andriuță, Adriana Titieni, and Tudor Istodor. Alexandru Talambă served as artistic director, while Didier Falk composed the music. Bogdan Mureșanu previously reached the Academy Awards shortlist with The Christmas Gift , which won best European short film at the 2019 European Film Awards. He is also the writer, director and producer of The New Year That Never Came, winner of the best film and FIPRESCI awards in the Orizzonti section of the 2024 Venice Film Festival.

data.title: Romanian railway company CFR seeks contractors for EUR 750 mln in maintenance works
data.description: The works aim to improve traffic safety and eliminate speed restrictions on railway infrastructure sections within the seven regions. According to the announcement published on Monday, October 19, in the Electronic Public Procurement System (SEAP), the procedure is divided into seven lots, corresponding to the Bucharest, Craiova, Timișoara, Cluj, Brașov, Galați and Constanța regions, Economica.net reported. The maximum estimated value of each lot is RON 584.5 million, excluding VAT. Seven framework agreements, each with a duration of 48 months, will be concluded following the tender. “The procurement procedure provides for the conclusion of framework agreements at the central level of CFR SA, while subsequent contracts for the actual execution of the works will be concluded at the level of the regional branches. Financing is provided from the state budget, under budget title 51 – ‘Maintenance and operation of public infrastructure’, relating to the railway directorate. The works will be contracted and executed based on identified needs and allocated funds,” CFR SA said in a press release. The value of RON 4.09 billion represents the maximum total estimated value of the seven framework agreements over the full four-year period, rather than the value of execution contracts already awarded, company representatives said.

data.title: Romania’s utility Electrica seeks EUR 355 mln in EIB financing
data.description: The company is considering one or more secured or unsecured loans, totalling up to EUR 355 million, under one or more credit agreements with the EIB, Economedia.ro reported. The funds will be used to finance and partially refinance the 2027–2030 investment plan of Electrica’s subsidiary Distribuție Energie Electrică România SA (DEER), which aims to modernise and digitise electricity distribution networks. Another objective is to develop a portfolio of battery storage installations at distributed locations. The project will have a total storage capacity of up to 800 MWh, with the investment estimated at a maximum of EUR 185 million, excluding VAT. Societatea Energetică Electrica SA (ELSA) has convened an Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (EGMS) for December 10, 2026.

data.title: Candidate transport minister pledges to keep Romania's flag carrier Tarom alive
data.description: The carrier will continue operating, Ștefan-Ovidiu Popa, the candidate for minister of transport and infrastructure, said during his hearing before the parliamentary committee on October 19. The incoming government’s programme envisages attracting a strategic investor to acquire a stake of 20–49%. “We will do everything possible” to extend the deadline set under the restructuring plan approved by the European Commission in 2024, he said, as reported by Profit.ro . “We will have to submit the revised reorganisation plan to the European Commission by December 31, 2026, and I can tell you right away that Tarom will not close. Tarom is a Romanian brand that must continue to exist. I will meet with the management, and we will establish the details from there,” the ministerial candidate said. The Luca Niculescu government will support a revised two-year business plan for the national carrier before the European Commission while also seeking to attract a strategic investor, either for a minority stake of 20-49% or for a majority stake, according to the governing programme of the prime minister-designate. “We support the revised two-year business plan before the European Commission, which must demonstrate Tarom’s viability by December 31, 2026, and protect the approved state aid of EUR 95.3 million. With the installation of professional management, we will conduct a transparent and competitive procedure in 2027 to attract a strategic investor (a minority stake of 20–49% or a majority stake), while maintaining technical maintenance services and essential domestic routes through competitively assigned public service obligations,” the government programme states.

data.title: Romanian construction group Erbașu builds EUR 17 mln recycling plant
data.description: Located in Ilfov County, near Bucharest, the plant can recycle concrete, bricks, mineral materials and glass, with an annual capacity of 450,000 tonnes, Profit.ro reported. The project received maximum grant financing of RON 39 million out of its total value of RON 87 million, according to the project specifications, as published by Fabricadereciclare.ro . BRD-SocGen co-financed the investment with a RON 61 million loan. The loan has a 10-year maturity and is aligned with the Loan Market Association’s (LMA) Green Loan Principles, according to BRD. The investment incorporates state-of-the-art equipment, electric machinery, IoT technologies, automated monitoring systems and an ERP platform, enabling the digitalisation and automation of more than 70% of the operational workflow. The sustainability component is further strengthened by the installation of more than 560 photovoltaic panels, rainwater reuse and high-performance systems designed to reduce dust emissions and improve energy efficiency. The plant can process more than 450,000 tonnes of construction and demolition waste annually, including approximately 410,000 tonnes of heavy fractions, mainly concrete and asphalt, and around 40,000 tonnes of light fractions, including wood, plastic, cardboard, paper, basalt wool, foil, polystyrene and metals. The project also includes a dedicated glass recycling line with an annual capacity of at least 1,200 tonnes. The technologies used are intended to maximise the recovery of construction and demolition waste and reduce the volume sent for disposal. The resulting products include recycled crushed concrete, recycled asphalt, shredded glass, metals and alternative fuel. A significant share of the recovered materials is reused in the Erbașu group’s own operations, helping to close the materials loop and reduce the consumption of natural resources.

data.title: Healthcare in Bucharest: A Practical Guide for Expats on Doctors, Insurance and Medical Emergencies
data.description: Moving to Bucharest involves more than finding a home, arranging residency documents and adapting to a new working environment. For expatriates and their families, understanding how to access healthcare is an equally important part of settling into life in Romania. The Romanian healthcare system combines publicly funded services with a well-developed private medical sector. What many newcomers do not realize is that these two systems frequently overlap: privately operated clinics can also provide consultations covered by the national health insurance system. For international residents, this means that finding appropriate medical care is often less about choosing between public and private providers and more about understanding insurance eligibility, referral requirements and available services. Medical networks such as Clinica Prevencia , which operates outpatient facilities across Bucharest, illustrate this combined approach by bringing together family medicine, specialist consultations and access to both publicly funded and privately paid healthcare. Understanding public and private healthcare in Romania Romania's public health insurance system is administered by the National Health Insurance House (CNAS), through regional and local health insurance institutions, including CASMB in Bucharest. People insured under the Romanian system can access a range of medical services through providers contracted with the relevant health insurance house. These may include family medicine, specialist consultations, diagnostic investigations and hospital treatment, subject to eligibility and applicable coverage conditions. An important distinction for newcomers is that private clinics are not necessarily private-pay-only facilities . Many independent medical providers have contracts with the public health insurance system, allowing eligible patients to receive certain services without paying directly for the consultation. Clinica Prevencia follows this model, providing both CAS-funded medical consultations and private-pay services across a range of specialties. However, not every consultation or investigation is automatically covered. Availability depends on the patient's insurance status, the medical service required and the provider's applicable contractual arrangements. Private medical insurance and employer-sponsored healthcare subscriptions offer additional options, although their coverage varies. International residents should review the specific terms of their policies rather than assume that all outpatient care is included. Can expats access healthcare through Romanian public insurance? Foreign citizenship does not, by itself, determine whether someone qualifies for Romanian public health insurance. Eligibility depends on employment, residency status, applicable social security arrangements and other legal conditions. Foreign nationals legally employed in Romania are generally covered through the applicable health insurance contribution system. Other residents may qualify under different provisions or require separate insurance arrangements. European Union citizens visiting Romania temporarily may use a valid European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) to access medically necessary state-provided healthcare under the relevant European rules. However, the EHIC is intended for temporary stays. People relocating to Romania should establish which national social security system is responsible for their healthcare coverage. For non-EU residents, insurance arrangements depend on their legal and employment circumstances. Before requesting a publicly funded medical appointment, foreign residents should verify their insurance status and confirm that the required service is covered. At Prevencia, insured patients can access a range of specialist services under the public health insurance system, subject to the relevant requirements. The clinic provides a practical explanation of CAS-funded medical consultations in Bucharest , including eligibility, referral documents and the specialties available. For expats unfamiliar with the Romanian system, checking these requirements before booking can help avoid unnecessary administrative difficulties. Finding a family doctor and accessing specialists For international residents planning to stay in Bucharest long-term, establishing a relationship with a family doctor is often a sensible first step. Known in Romanian as a medic de familie , the family doctor provides primary medical care, monitors chronic conditions, offers preventive services and helps coordinate access to specialist treatment. For many specialist consultations covered through CAS, patients generally need a referral known as a bilet de trimitere . Certain medical conditions and specialties are exceptions to this requirement. Private-pay consultations can usually be booked directly, without a referral, although an initial medical assessment may still be necessary. The choice of medical specialist depends on the patient's symptoms and medical history. Cardiologists assess cardiovascular conditions, dermatologists evaluate skin disorders, endocrinologists investigate hormonal problems, and psychiatrists provide medical care for mental health conditions. When symptoms are unclear or involve several possible medical conditions, a family doctor or internal medicine specialist can help determine the appropriate next steps. Clinica Prevencia operates a multidisciplinary outpatient network , bringing together family medicine and specialties such as internal medicine, cardiology, dermatology, endocrinology, psychiatry, neurology, orthopedics and medical rehabilitation. For patients managing ongoing health conditions, access to several medical specialties within the same network can simplify follow-up appointments and improve continuity of care. Specialty availability and insurance coverage may differ between clinics, making it advisable to confirm the relevant details in advance. Language barriers: an overlooked healthcare challenge For expatriates, finding a doctor is only part of the challenge. Understanding medical instructions, insurance procedures, referral documents and the terminology used during consultations can be equally important. Even foreign residents who communicate comfortably in everyday Romanian may find medical discussions and administrative requirements difficult to navigate. Recognizing this challenge, Prevencia has developed "Prevencia for All," an initiative providing free practical healthcare guides in 22 languages for people arriving in Romania from abroad. The guides explain how the healthcare system works, which documents patients may need and what to expect when visiting a medical clinic. Available languages include English, German, Arabic, Turkish, Ukrainian, Hindi, Chinese and several others, reflecting the diversity of international communities living and working in Romania. The initiative addresses a practical need: helping patients understand the healthcare system before they need medical attention. Prevencia also provides assistance in Romanian and English. Patients who require an English-speaking physician should confirm language availability when arranging their appointment. For international employers relocating staff to Bucharest, access to understandable healthcare information can also help employees and their families navigate the transition more easily. Choosing a convenient medical provider in Bucharest Location and accessibility are important considerations, particularly for working professionals, families with children and patients who require regular medical monitoring. Bucharest's size and traffic can make travelling between unrelated medical providers inconvenient. Choosing a multidisciplinary clinic can reduce some of these difficulties by allowing patients to access several specialties within an established healthcare network. Clinica Prevencia operates a growing network of outpatient medical facilities across Bucharest, bringing together family medicine and a broad range of medical specialties. Patients can choose a convenient location based on their healthcare needs while benefiting from access to multiple services within the same medical network. Appointments can be arranged through Prevencia's online medical booking platform , where patients can review available specialties, physicians and clinic locations. For patients transferring their medical care from another country, it is useful to keep previous medical reports, prescriptions, laboratory results and information about existing conditions readily available. These records can help physicians understand medical history and determine whether additional investigations are necessary. Medical emergencies and private ambulance services Understanding how emergency medical assistance works is essential for anyone living in Romania. The national emergency number is 112. It should be used for potentially life-threatening situations, including suspected heart attack or stroke, severe breathing difficulties, loss of consciousness, major trauma or other serious medical emergencies. The public emergency response system coordinates the appropriate intervention. Private ambulance operators provide additional medical assistance options, which may include medically assisted transport, home-based healthcare services and medical support for events. Ambulanta PULS, part of the Prevencia group, operates a private ambulance service available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Its services include medically assisted transport within Romania and internationally, selected medical assistance at home and medical support for events. These options may be relevant for patients who require supervised transport following hospital discharge, people with reduced mobility or families arranging planned medical assistance. Information about the available services can be found through Ambulanta PULS . Patients should confirm the medical suitability, availability and costs of private ambulance services directly with the operator. Private ambulance arrangements should not delay contacting 112 in a suspected life-threatening emergency. Five practical steps before your first medical appointment Navigating healthcare in Bucharest becomes considerably easier when a few basic arrangements are made in advance. 1. Verify your insurance status. Establish whether you are covered through Romanian public health insurance, another applicable European social security arrangement, private insurance or an employer-sponsored healthcare subscription. 2. Identify a family doctor. For long-term residents eligible to register, a family doctor can coordinate routine healthcare, preventive services and specialist referrals. 3. Understand referral requirements. Many consultations funded through CAS require a valid referral, while private-pay appointments generally offer direct access to specialists. 4. Prepare your medical documents. Keep identification, relevant insurance documentation, previous medical records and a current list of medications accessible. Ask in advance whether an English-speaking physician is available. 5. Know your emergency options. Save 112 for serious medical emergencies and understand which non-emergency medical assistance and transport services are available when needed. Taking these steps before a medical problem occurs can reduce uncertainty and make accessing healthcare more straightforward. Making healthcare in Bucharest easier to navigate Romania offers multiple pathways to medical care, but understanding how they fit together is particularly important for foreign residents. Public insurance can provide access to a wide range of services, including through privately operated medical facilities, while private-pay consultations and additional medical assistance services offer other options depending on individual needs. For expats and international families, choosing a provider that combines primary care, medical specialties and clear information about insurance requirements can simplify the experience. Clinica Prevencia represents one such option in Bucharest , combining multidisciplinary outpatient care with access to CAS-funded services and practical information designed to help international patients understand the Romanian healthcare system. Through initiatives such as Prevencia for All , the network also addresses an important aspect of healthcare accessibility that is often overlooked: the ability of patients to understand how to obtain care in a country whose language and administrative procedures may be unfamiliar. Ultimately, accessing healthcare in a new country becomes easier when patients understand their coverage, establish reliable medical contacts and know where to turn when assistance is needed. For international residents settling in Bucharest, that preparation is an important part of making the city feel like home.

Certain medical conditions and specialties are exceptions to this requirement. Private-pay consultations can usually be booked directly, without a referral, although an initial medical assessment may still be necessary. The choice of medical specialist depends on the patient's symptoms and medical history. Cardiologists assess cardiovascular conditions, dermatologists evaluate skin disorders, endocrinologists investigate hormonal problems, and psychiatrists provide medical care for mental health conditions. When symptoms are unclear or involve several possible medical conditions, a family doctor or internal medicine specialist can help determine the appropriate next steps. Clinica Prevencia operates a multidisciplinary outpatient network , bringing together family medicine and specialties such as internal medicine, cardiology, dermatology, endocrinology, psychiatry, neurology, orthopedics and medical rehabilitation. For patients managing ongoing health conditions, access to several medical specialties within the same network can simplify follow-up appointments and improve continuity of care. Specialty availability and insurance coverage may differ between clinics, making it advisable to confirm the relevant details in advance. Language barriers: an overlooked healthcare challenge For expatriates, finding a doctor is only part of the challenge. Understanding medical instructions, insurance procedures, referral documents and the terminology used during consultations can be equally important. Even foreign residents who communicate comfortably in everyday Romanian may find medical discussions and administrative requirements difficult to navigate. Recognizing this challenge, Prevencia has developed "Prevencia for All," an initiative providing free practical healthcare guides in 22 languages for people arriving in Romania from abroad. The guides explain how the healthcare system works, which documents patients may need and what to expect when visiting a medical clinic. Available languages include English, German, Arabic, Turkish, Ukrainian, Hindi, Chinese and several others, reflecting the diversity of international communities living and working in Romania. The initiative addresses a practical need: helping patients understand the healthcare system before they need medical attention. Prevencia also provides assistance in Romanian and English. Patients who require an English-speaking physician should confirm language availability when arranging their appointment. For international employers relocating staff to Bucharest, access to understandable healthcare information can also help employees and their families navigate the transition more easily. Choosing a convenient medical provider in Bucharest Location and accessibility are important considerations, particularly for working professionals, families with children and patients who require regular medical monitoring. Bucharest's size and traffic can make travelling between unrelated medical providers inconvenient. Choosing a multidisciplinary clinic can reduce some of these difficulties by allowing patients to access several specialties within an established healthcare network. Clinica Prevencia operates a growing network of outpatient medical facilities across Bucharest, bringing together family medicine and a broad range of medical specialties. Patients can choose a convenient location based on their healthcare needs while benefiting from access to multiple services within the same medical network. Appointments can be arranged through Prevencia's online medical booking platform , where patients can review available specialties, physicians and clinic locations. For patients transferring their medical care from another country, it is useful to keep previous medical reports, prescriptions, laboratory results and information about existing conditions readily available. These records can help physicians understand medical history and determine whether additional investigations are necessary. Medical emergencies and private ambulance services Understanding how emergency medical assistance works is essential for anyone living in Romania. The national emergency number is 112. It should be used for potentially life-threatening situations, including suspected heart attack or stroke, severe breathing difficulties, loss of consciousness, major trauma or other serious medical emergencies. The public emergency response system coordinates the appropriate intervention. Private ambulance operators provide additional medical assistance options, which may include medically assisted transport, home-based healthcare services and medical support for events. Ambulanta PULS, part of the Prevencia group, operates a private ambulance service available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Its services include medically assisted transport within Romania and internationally, selected medical assistance at home and medical support for events. These options may be relevant for patients who require supervised transport following hospital discharge, people with reduced mobility or families arranging planned medical assistance. Information about the available services can be found through Ambulanta PULS . Patients should confirm the medical suitability, availability and costs of private ambulance services directly with the operator. Private ambulance arrangements should not delay contacting 112 in a suspected life-threatening emergency. Five practical steps before your first medical appointment Navigating healthcare in Bucharest becomes considerably easier when a few basic arrangements are made in advance. 1. Verify your insurance status. Establish whether you are covered through Romanian public health insurance, another applicable European social security arrangement, private insurance or an employer-sponsored healthcare subscription. 2. Identify a family doctor. For long-term residents eligible to register, a family doctor can coordinate routine healthcare, preventive services and specialist referrals. 3. Understand referral requirements. Many consultations funded through CAS require a valid referral, while private-pay appointments generally offer direct access to specialists. 4. Prepare your medical documents. Keep identification, relevant insurance documentation, previous medical records and a current list of medications accessible. Ask in advance whether an English-speaking physician is available. 5. Know your emergency options. Save 112 for serious medical emergencies and understand which non-emergency medical assistance and transport services are available when needed. Taking these steps before a medical problem occurs can reduce uncertainty and make accessing healthcare more straightforward. Making healthcare in Bucharest easier to navigate Romania offers multiple pathways to medical care, but understanding how they fit together is particularly important for foreign residents. Public insurance can provide access to a wide range of services, including through privately operated medical facilities, while private-pay consultations and additional medical assistance services offer other options depending on individual needs. For expats and international families, choosing a provider that combines primary care, medical specialties and clear information about insurance requirements can simplify the experience. Clinica Prevencia represents one such option in Bucharest , combining multidisciplinary outpatient care with access to CAS-funded services and practical information designed to help international patients understand the Romanian healthcare system. Through initiatives such as Prevencia for All , the network also addresses an important aspect of healthcare accessibility that is often overlooked: the ability of patients to understand how to obtain care in a country whose language and administrative procedures may be unfamiliar. Ultimately, accessing healthcare in a new country becomes easier when patients understand their coverage, establish reliable medical contacts and know where to turn when assistance is needed. For international residents settling in Bucharest, that preparation is an important part of making the city feel like home.

data.title: Danube at Romania’s Cernavoda nuclear power plant below ‘critical’ safety level for three days, five more to follow
data.description: The level is forecast to remain below the threshold for another five days, News.ro reported. According to available information, no special measures have been taken, aside from the suspension of traffic on the Danube-Black Sea Canal, to make more water available to the NPP. Authorities have previously explained that a fall below this threshold could pose an ‘operational risk’ to the supply of water needed to cool the plant’s reactors. According to measurements by the Lower Danube River Administration (AFDJ), the Danube level at Cernavoda stood at -262 cm on Saturday, October 17, -266 cm on Sunday and -268 cm on Monday. The critical threshold is -262 cm, measured against the so-called ‘zero elevation’ - the conventional reference level established at each hydrometric station against which the height of the river is measured. AFDJ expects the Danube level at Cernavoda to remain below the critical threshold for another five days. In this context, News.ro asked government representatives, interim transport minister Radu Miruță, representatives of Nuclearelectrica and the National Commission for Nuclear Activities Control what measures were being taken to ensure the safe operation of the Cernavoda NPP. However, the news outlet said it received no response. In a document sent to the Bucharest Stock Exchange last week, the nuclear power plant’s operator, Nuclearelectrica (BVB: SNN), announced that both reactors were being maintained in a safe shutdown state. The company said the current situation posed no risk to nuclear safety and that the plant had several cooling systems designed to operate at different cooling-water levels, which are activated and used according to specific technical parameters. Nuclear safety functions are therefore fully ensured at all times, the company emphasised, adding that the units would remain in a safe shutdown state until the Danube level allowed operations to resume safely. The only institution to provide a statement on the critically low Danube level at the Cernavoda NPP was the National Administration ‘Romanian Waters’, which said that water levels were expected to rise after October 23 and that use of the Danube-Black Sea Canal for transport had been suspended to secure more water for the NPP. "Following an analysis of the forecasts, which indicate a slight upward trend after October 23, and inter-institutional discussions, it was decided to reduce the flow allocated to transport on the Danube-Black Sea Canal. This will maintain levels in the Cernavoda section that continue to allow optimal water intake for the cooling systems of the Cernavoda NPP," officials from the National Administration ‘Romanian Waters’ told News.ro. The locks will therefore be opened only for transport considered essential, they said. "Consequently, no additional operational pumping procedures are required on the [Cernavoda NPP] site," they concluded.

data.title: Luca Niculescu’s proposed government faces confidence vote in Romanian Parliament
data.description: Prime minister-designate Luca Niculescu will present his proposed government and governing program to Romania’s Parliament on Tuesday, October 20. The joint session of the Chamber of Deputies and Senate is scheduled to begin at 2 p.m. Niculescu’s proposed 18-member cabinet includes 11 ministers from the Social Democratic Party (PSD) and seven independents. PSD, the National Liberal Party (PNL), the Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania (UDMR), the national minorities group, and the United for Romania parliamentary group have announced their support for the cabinet. Together, they could deliver 279 votes, comfortably above the 233 required for confirmation, Hotnews.ro noted. On the other hand, the far-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR) and the reformist Save Romania Union (USR) have said they will vote against the proposed government. PNL and UDMR have signed agreements with Luca Niculescu, although they will not hold ministerial positions in the proposed cabinet and intend to move into opposition. Under parliamentary procedure, Luca Niculescu will present his ministers and governing program before lawmakers debate the proposal. Deputies and senators will then vote by secret ballot, with an absolute majority of all lawmakers required for the government to take office. President Nicușor Dan nominated Niculescu for prime minister on October 5 . He is the fourth nominee since Liberal leader Ilie Bolojan’s government was removed by a no-confidence motion on May 5 . The first nominee, Eugen Tomac, withdrew before seeking Parliament’s approval. The following two nominees, Adrian Veștea and Siegfried Mureșan , failed to secure sufficient support in confidence votes. If confirmed, the Luca Niculescu cabinet would end more than five months in which Romania has been governed without a fully empowered executive.

data.title: Romanian leaders discuss rule of law with Venice Commission delegation
data.description: President Nicușor Dan reaffirmed Romania’s commitment to institutional balance, transparency, and European democratic standards during talks with a Venice Commission delegation. The meeting addressed the rule of law, the role of democratic institutions, and respect for constitutional principles, he announced. “Open dialogue with European experts is essential,” president Dan wrote on Facebook. “During the meeting, we reaffirmed our commitment to institutional balance, transparency and compliance with European standards on democracy and the rule of law.” https://www.facebook.com/NicusorDan.ro/posts/pfbid022VhFoHWjrqL7cJGo2pwi1pQ1ALhvrWmjD3GnnjRX6uzMFvCDLay69umEoJVhMKBzl The delegation from the European Commission for Democracy through Law, better known as the Venice Commission, was led by its president, Marta Cartabia. Its visit coincided with the second edition of a rule-of-law forum held in Romania. Cartabia and the delegation also met interim prime minister Ilie Bolojan at Victoria Palace in Bucharest. Their talks focused on the justice system and the need to rebuild public confidence in state institutions, the government announced . “The quality of justice is closely linked to the quality of legislation, but also to its interpretation,” Bolojan said. “If there is no consistency, balance, and predictability in decisions, citizens’ trust in state institutions declines.” The prime minister thanked the Venice Commission for its expertise and continuing support, adding that Romania still needs the partnership. During the meeting, Marta Cartabia presented Ilie Bolojan with a copy of the commission’s updated Rule of Law Checklist. The document provides criteria intended to support objective, transparent, and comparable assessments of countries’ adherence to rule-of-law principles. The Venice Commission is an advisory body of the Council of Europe that provides constitutional and legal expertise to member states.

data.title: Arcub brings “Israel & Mohamed” to Bucharest for its international theatre season
data.description: Israel & Mohamed , a production that premiered at the 2025 Avignon Festival and has since been presented on major European stages, will be performed in Bucharest for the opening of the fall program of Arcub’s International Theater Season. Created by Zirlib and IGalván Company, the production brings together flamenco dancer and choreographer Israel Galván and French writer and director Mohamed El Khatib. Born in Seville into a family of dancers, Israel Galván is one of the leading figures in contemporary flamenco. He has collaborated with artists including Akram Khan and Marlene Monteiro Freitas; he received Spain's Premio Nacional de Danza and the New York Bessie Performance Award, and was named an Officer of France's Order of Arts and Letters in 2016. Mohamed El Khatib, a French writer, director, producer, and visual artist of Moroccan origin, works at the intersection of theatre, literature, film, and visual arts, drawing inspiration from documentary practice. His works often stem from personal experiences and real-life stories, which he transforms into reflections on family, memory, and contemporary society. In Israel & Mohamed , the two artists “bring their respective worlds, artistic practices, and personal journeys closer together in a dialogue where differences prove just as fertile as common ground.” Beyond its intimate dimension, Israel & Mohamed becomes a living archive of personal stories, historical moments, and the history of dance. “Israel Galván and Mohamed El Khatib represent artistic disciplines and worlds that seem very different, yet on stage they find a language at their intersection, a polyphonic one in which movement, gesture, words, and filmed images converge around a common point: the rift between generations. Their dialogue is, at its core, a conversation with their fathers and with the latter's difficulty in accepting the reality and choices of their sons," Oana Borș, curator of the Arcub International Theatre Season, explains. "With humor, self-irony, and sometimes sadness, the two artists turn these wounds into stage material. Beyond its intimate dimension, Israel & Mohamed becomes a living archive of personal stories, historical moments, and the history of dance, while also offering a journey into Mohamed El Khatib's poetic universe,” she added. The 2026 edition of Arcub’s International Theatre Season, themed “Crisis/Crises,” highlights "intergenerational tensions and the conflict between inherited legacies and the freedom to shape one's own identity." The performance is scheduled for October 23 and October 24 at Arcub – Hanul Gabroveni. It is presented in French and Spanish, with Romanian and English surtitles. The October 23 performance will be followed by a Q&A session moderated by director Theodor Cristian Popescu, as part of the “Artist to Artist” program.

data.title: British-Romanian director Rachel Tâpârjan wins British Film Institute award
data.description: British-Romanian director Rachel Tâpârjan has received the BFI & CHANEL Filmmaker Award for her documentary Something Familiar . The award is granted by the British Film Institute (BFI) in partnership with CHANEL to filmmakers selected for their “creative audacity and ambition to explore a new dynamic to their practice.” Rachel Tâpârjan is one of four filmmakers honored this year, selected by a jury that included Oscar-winning actress Jessie Buckley, recognized for her role in Hamnet , and Emmy-nominated actress Gwendoline Christie, known for playing Brienne of Tarth in Game of Thrones , alongside Edward Enninful OBE, former editor-in-chief of British Vogue; producer Marie-Louise Khondji; and Ben Roberts, the BFI's chief executive. It was the film that stayed with us the longest, and impossible to stop thinking about. In explaining its decision, the jury highlighted the director's courage in laying bare her own story and the way it takes on new meanings as the film unfolds. “We wanted to celebrate Rachel’s bravery and total openness – a naked, unself-conscious revelation of self. A deceptively simple search for family that opens onto identity, inheritance and generational trauma, using camera, narration and interviews which all keep shifting the viewer’s understanding. It was the film that stayed with us the longest, and impossible to stop thinking about,” the jury said. More than anything, the award has made me feel that I can be ambitious about the kind of filmmaker I want to become. “Receiving the BFI & CHANEL Filmmaker Award has meant an enormous amount to me. Something Familiar is my first feature documentary, and making it required a huge amount of trust, care and belief from the people involved. To have the film and my work recognized in this way has given me real confidence as I move towards my next projects. More than anything, the award has made me feel that I can be ambitious about the kind of filmmaker I want to become,” Rachel Tâpârjan said. Still from "Something Familiar" Tâpârjan, who was adopted from Romania as a child and grew up in the UK, holds a PhD in social work and teaches at Teesside University in northeast England. Her professional work focuses on trauma and support for vulnerable people. Her short films have screened at festivals including Sheffield DocFest, the East End Film Festival, and the SEE Film Festival. Something Familiar is her feature documentary debut. The feature-length documentary, a Romanian-British co-production, began its international festival run in the DOX competition at CPH 2026. The film subsequently received the Hera “Nuovi Talenti” Special Mention in the International Competition at the 2026 Biografilm Festival. It opens in Romanian cinemas on November 13, distributed by Filmways. The documentary centers on Rachel and Mihaela, two young women who were adopted as children from the same orphanage in Romania. One grew up in the UK, the other in Canada. Years later, Mihaela asks Rachel to help her find her biological mother. Their return to Romania, however, opens up another search: the director's own, as she uncovers a family history far more complicated than she could have imagined. Filmed over six years, the documentary follows their searches and the discoveries that change their course. https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dee0P1dAbEz/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link Something Familiar is produced by Romania's Manifest Film, through Monica Lăzurean-Gorgan and Elena Martin, in co-production with UK-based My Accomplice. The film was made with support from the National Film Center of Romania (CNC), in collaboration with Romanian Television (TVR). The project received support from BFI & Doc Society through the BFI Doc Society Fund, as well as Creative Europe MEDIA, CIRCLE Women Doc Accelerator, and Chicken & Egg Films.
