data.title: Exhibition explores Bucharest fashion from the 19th century to the 1940s
data.description: Dressing Time: Bucharest – Fashion, Memory, Identity , an exhibition open at Arcub, explores the evolution of clothing and the social and cultural transformations of Romania's capital from the mid-19th century to the 1940s. Curated by Iulia Gorneanu, the exhibition gathers around 1,000 items to build a journey through Bucharest's history through clothing, accessories, photographs, and publications from the period. It features garments, hats, fans, accessories, dance cards, photographs, and period publications from the private collections of those behind its curatorial concept, namely Iulia Gorneanu, Valentin and Raluca Partenie, and Andreea Ciortea. Photo: Arcub “More than an exploration of fashion history, Dressing Time examines how changes in clothing accompanied transformations in Bucharest society, from the gradual move away from Eastern influences towards Western styles to women's emancipation and the emergence of a modern urban identity,” the organizers explain. Photo: Arcub The exhibition also highlights the role of magazines, cinema, and theatre in shaping fashion tastes. Publications such as Realitatea Ilustrată and Ilustrațiunea Română, featured in the exhibition, document the vibrancy of social life and how Bucharest residents followed the latest trends. Outfits worn at horse races, theatre and film premieres, and events in the capital's grand salons became sources of inspiration for the public and the city's tailor shops. The exhibition is on view at Hanul Gabroveni's Sala Arcelor and Sala Librărie until October 31. Access is free.
data.translatedTitle: Exhibition explores Bucharest fashion from the 19th century to the 1940s
data.translatedDescription: Dressing Time: Bucharest – Fashion, Memory, Identity , an exhibition open at Arcub, explores the evolution of clothing and the social and cultural transformations of Romania's capital from the mid-19th century to the 1940s. Curated by Iulia Gorneanu, the exhibition gathers around 1,000 items to build a journey through Bucharest's history through clothing, accessories, photographs, and publications from the period. It features garments, hats, fans, accessories, dance cards, photographs, and period publications from the private collections of those behind its curatorial concept, namely Iulia Gorneanu, Valentin and Raluca Partenie, and Andreea Ciortea. Photo: Arcub “More than an exploration of fashion history, Dressing Time examines how changes in clothing accompanied transformations in Bucharest society, from the gradual move away from Eastern influences towards Western styles to women's emancipation and the emergence of a modern urban identity,” the organizers explain. Photo: Arcub The exhibition also highlights the role of magazines, cinema, and theatre in shaping fashion tastes. Publications such as Realitatea Ilustrată and Ilustrațiunea Română, featured in the exhibition, document the vibrancy of social life and how Bucharest residents followed the latest trends. Outfits worn at horse races, theatre and film premieres, and events in the capital's grand salons became sources of inspiration for the public and the city's tailor shops. The exhibition is on view at Hanul Gabroveni's Sala Arcelor and Sala Librărie until October 31. Access is free.

data.title: Romania’s winter time change in 2026: When to turn back the clocks
data.description: Romania is set to change to winter time to benefit from more natural light. The time change takes place twice a year, in spring and autumn. The upcoming switch to winter time takes place during the night, on the last weekend of October, from October 24 to 25. The change involves moving clocks back by 60 minutes. For devices connected to the internet, such as mobile phones, computers and smartwatches, the update is generally performed automatically, if the settings allow it. By contrast, wall clocks, wristwatches and certain electronic devices must be adjusted manually. The return to standard time ends the period during which Romania used daylight saving time. The change applies nationwide. The original purpose of this practice was to make more efficient use of natural light and reduce electricity consumption. At the European Union level, the time change is regulated through a common system applied in member states. Although abandoning seasonal clock changes has been discussed within European institutions, the system remains in force. The idea of adapting the daily schedule to natural light has a longer history than the modern daylight saving time system. In 1784, Benjamin Franklin suggested changing working hours to reduce the use of candles. Later, in 1895, New Zealander George Hudson proposed changing the time to benefit from more daylight after the end of the working day, according to ProTV . The first official implementation of daylight saving time took place in 1916, in Germany and Austria-Hungary, during World War I. The measure aimed to save energy resources, particularly coal used for energy production and lighting.

data.title: Germany’s Rheinmetall announces plans for major military shipbuilding hub at Romania’s Mangalia shipyard
data.description: Rheinmetall, the German defense giant valued at roughly EUR 50 billion, confirmed its intention to acquire the Romanian Mangalia shipyard, located south of Constanța, together with Swiss shipping company MSC. Damen Shipyards Mangalia was awarded to Rheinmetall Real Estate Romania on Friday, October 9, in an auction organized by judicial liquidator CITR, for EUR 138 million, excluding VAT. The Romanian government also welcomed the approval of the acquisition. With a delay of 10 days, the company noted that it had been awarded the bid following an auction and that the acquisition is expected to be finalized within a few weeks. “The takeover aims to establish a dual-use production site, where both civil and military shipbuilding activities for domestic and international markets can be developed and carried out in parallel. To this end, the site will be subdivided into various sectors and security zones in the future,” the company said in a press release. Rheinmetall also said that the Mangalia shipyard will play an important role in the build of four naval vessels, which have been commissioned by the Romanian government. The ships include “two 96-metre offshore patrol vessels as well as two 43-metre diver support vessels.” At the same time, the site is intended to serve as a hub for further military shipbuilding projects. In doing so, Rheinmetall is creating a scalable foundation for future projects in south-eastern Europe and strengthening its position in a strategically important market. “Following the acquisition, we plan to expand and upgrade the shipyard comprehensively. We aim to further develop the existing infrastructure, improve production conditions and adapt capacity to meet future requirements. This will enable the site in the long term to play a key role in the implementation of our strategic activities in South-Eastern Europe and to strengthen our industrial presence in the region,” said Tim Wagner, CEO of the Naval Systems division. The sale price of the Mangalia shipyard was at 75% of the EUR 184 million market value used for the previous four auctions. Those attempts ended without a buyer. Damen Shipyards Mangalia entered insolvency on June 19, 2024, following a request from its parent company, Damen Holding BV.

data.title: Bucharest’s UNDERCLOUD festival announces 19 productions over 10 days
data.description: The UNDERCLOUD Independent Theater Festival will hold its 19th edition in Bucharest from November 2 through 11. Its program features 19 productions ranging from reinterpretations of classical texts to experimental and interdisciplinary performances. The festival opens on November 2 with Funny Games , directed by Botond Nagy and starring Ofelia Popii. Adapted from Michael Haneke’s film, the 100-minute production examines violence, spectatorship and the increasingly blurred boundary between victim and aggressor. Then, on November 3, Nicoleta Lefter stars in Alin Uberti’s production of Antigone . The program that week also includes Femina , directed by Tamara Găgeatu; Jocuri în curtea din spate , directed by Ioana Barbu; Umami , directed by Teodora Savu; and Trap by Bogdan Georgescu. Several productions will highlight short and experimental formats, including Andrei Bouariu’s Împlinirea tuturor dorințelor și alte accidente , Geo Vișan’s Liminal - Zgomotul din care tac, and Andreea Agapi and Raluca Cristea’s În mintea Aglajei . The November 7 program includes Alexandra Pribeagu’s Suflet de copil , a production recommended for audiences ages 10 to 100, followed by Teodora Savu’s black comedy Menada . On November 8, Gabriel Scalschi presents The Seagull by K. Treplev , a new interpretation of Chekhov’s play. Botond Nagy returns on November 9 with Medea’s Children , based on Milo Rau’s text, which combines Euripides’ tragedy with a real-life case. Other productions in the closing days include Natural Disasters , directed by Alexandru Buescu, and Monica Stoica’s Rostopasca . The festival will end on November 11 with the UNDERCLOUD awards gala, followed by Madame Pylinska and the Secret of Chopin . Directed and adapted by Chris Simion-Mercurian from Éric-Emmanuel Schmitt’s work, the Grivița 53 Theater production stars Emilia Popescu and Luca Rusu and features Chopin’s music performed live. This year’s performances will also use the newly opened Grivița 53 Theater . Award-winning productions without a permanent venue may be included in the theater’s future season, festival founder Chris Simion-Mercurian said. Founded in 2008, UNDERCLOUD is Romania’s first independent theater festival. Tickets and age restrictions for individual productions are available on the festival’s website .

data.title: Zelensky asks Romania and neighbors to allow transit of Ukrainian grain shipments
data.description: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky asked Romania, Poland, Slovakia and Hungary to allow the transit of Ukrainian grain shipments to other markets at an EU summit in Brussels on Friday, October 16, according to Hungarian PM Peter Magyar. "Zelensky asked Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Hungary and all neighboring countries to allow transit, as they did three or four years ago, at the beginning of the war," Magyar said, cited by Profit.ro . Ukraine is among the world's largest producers of wheat, corn and sunflower seeds, and approximately 90% of exports of these products are usually transported through the Black Sea. Russia's campaign of attacks has, however, almost completely paralyzed agricultural shipments from Ukrainian ports. The Hungarian prime minister said the Ukrainian president had explained to him during a bilateral meeting that transporting corn in sealed trains to Western Europe would provide significant support for Ukraine's economy. Magyar, who agreed to relaunch bilateral relations with Ukraine the same day, said in a follow-up interview that Hungary would not oppose Ukrainian grain shipments, provided they transit through the country's territory without being sold on the local market. Kyiv's request comes as drought and extreme temperatures severely affected the European Union's corn production. The European Commission estimated at the end of August that the EU's corn harvest would fall to 50.1 million tons this year, the lowest level in almost two decades and approximately 20% below the average of the past three years. Farmers in France and Hungary are among those most affected by extreme weather conditions, which have damaged a significant proportion of corn crops. Both Moscow and Kyiv have expanded attacks on key sources of revenue, with Ukrainian forces targeting Russian energy infrastructure, including oil tankers, while Russia has intensified attacks on Black Sea ports. In April, Nikolai Patrushev, an adviser to Russian president Vladimir Putin and chairman of the Maritime Board, said that Romania had become a central hub for NATO's hostile operations against Russia in the Black Sea. "The Alliance continues to create anti-Russian infrastructure in the Black Sea direction, using Romania as a base," Patrushev said. He claimed that the main risks in the region were generated by Ukraine, which he accused of mining the area and using maritime drones to control naval traffic. According to his statements, mines that had broken loose from the area around Ukrainian ports had reached waters near the coasts of Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania. Earlier this month, Romania took steps to amend the rules governing the acceptance of freight trains at railway stations serving the Port of Constanta in a bid to streamline exports of Romanian grain.

data.title: Ireland sends 24 Romanian nationals back to Bucharest following criminal convictions
data.description: Ireland removed 24 Romanian nationals under EU free-movement rules following the completion of custodial sentences for criminal offenses. The charter flight left Dublin on October 18 and arrived in Bucharest later that evening, as announced by Ireland’s Department of Justice, Home Affairs, and Migration. The men were between 24 and 57 years old. Irish authorities did not provide details about their convictions. “Restricting the right to freedom of movement of European citizens is not a measure I take lightly, but there must be consequences if a person’s criminal behavior means they should no longer be entitled to access this privilege,” justice minister Jim O’Callaghan said. “I will take action if our laws are not upheld, and this includes enforcing removal orders for individuals who are a danger to the public,” he added. The operation was conducted in cooperation with Ireland’s prison service and national police. Police officers, medical personnel, interpreters, and a human rights observer accompanied the men on the flight. The aircraft cost EUR 182,270, excluding VAT, for the operation, according to the ministry. The flight brought the number of people removed from Ireland under the EU Free Movement Directive to 148 in 2026. Ireland has conducted seven removal charter flights this year, carrying a total of 245 people, including 91 EU citizens removed on grounds related to criminality. Minister of state Colm Brophy noted that the operation should not be seen as reflecting on Ireland’s wider Romanian community. “It is important to acknowledge that the majority of Romanian nationals resident in the State respect our laws and make a positive contribution to Irish society,” he said. Under Irish regulations implementing the EU Free Movement Directive, authorities may order the removal of an EU citizen or qualifying family member whose conduct represents a genuine and sufficiently serious threat to public policy, security, or health. An exclusion order can also prohibit the person from returning to Ireland for up to 10 years.

data.title: Flying Tiger Copenhagen plans expansion into Romania with BALFIN Group
data.description: BALFIN Group and Flying Tiger Copenhagen said they are expanding their partnership into Romania, Bulgaria, and Croatia. The rollout will begin in Romania and Bulgaria in 2027, followed by Croatia in early 2028. The companies did not disclose how the planned 87 stores would be divided among the three markets or provide details about their locations and investment value. The agreement builds on their existing partnership in Albania, Kosovo, North Macedonia, and Serbia, where they expect to operate a combined network of 20 stores by the end of 2026. They also plan to enter Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro in early 2027. “The results achieved with Flying Tiger Copenhagen have demonstrated the strength of our partnership and the potential for further growth,” said BALFIN Group president Samir Mane. “Expanding into Romania, Bulgaria, and Croatia takes our cooperation to a new level and brings the brand into three important EU markets.” Flying Tiger Copenhagen managing director for IMEA Julius Schmidt said the expansion is a natural next step following the performance of the partnership’s existing stores. “These are important markets for our European growth strategy, and we see significant potential for the Flying Tiger Copenhagen concept,” he stated. Founded in Copenhagen in 1995, Flying Tiger Copenhagen operates more than 1,100 stores across over 45 markets. The variety retailer sells products including toys, stationery, home accessories, kitchen items, and party supplies. BALFIN Group was established in Vienna in 1993 and has operations in 13 countries. The investment group employs approximately 5,000 people and has interests in retail, real estate, financial services, hospitality, logistics, energy, and other sectors.

data.title: R.Power completes construction of 55 MWp solar farm in northwestern Romania
data.description: European independent power producer R.Power announced that it completed construction of its 55 MWp Lazuri photovoltaic project in northwestern Romania. The company is now preparing the solar farm for energization and the start of commercial operations. Located in Satu Mare county, the project comprises 88,708 photovoltaic modules and six medium-voltage stations. Once operational, it is expected to generate approximately 70 GWh of electricity annually, making it one of Romania’s largest solar farms by installed capacity. “Completing construction works at Lazuri is an important milestone for R.Power’s Romanian solar portfolio,” said Florin Federenciuc, R.Power’s country head for Romania. “The project has moved efficiently from development through financing and construction, and we are now preparing for energization and the start of operations.” The Lazuri project secured a 15-year contract for difference from the Romanian authorities, providing long-term revenue predictability, the company said. It was financed through a EUR 44 million project finance facility signed by R.Power with ING Bank and UniCredit Bank in June 2026. The financing covers a portfolio of four Romanian solar projects with a combined capacity of approximately 75 MWp. “Romania remains a key market in our Central and Eastern European strategy, and we look forward to Lazuri contributing utility-scale clean energy to the grid,” Federenciuc added. R.Power has a 1.5 GW pipeline of solar, hybrid, and energy-storage projects in Romania. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Warsaw, the company has 1.9 GW of renewable-energy projects operating or under construction across Europe.

data.title: Magnitude 4.8 earthquake hits Romania
data.description: A magnitude 4.8 earthquake struck Romania’s Vrancea seismic region at 11:51 a.m. on Monday, October 19, according to the National Institute for Earth Physics (INCDFP). The quake occurred in Buzău County at a depth of 124.1 kilometers. The epicenter was located 54 km south of Buzău, 58 km east of Brașov, 60 km southeast of Sfântu Gheorghe, and 62 km north of Ploiești. It was also 72 km south of Focșani and 90 km northeast of Târgoviște. According to comments on the Institute's website, the earthquake was felt in Bucharest, as well as cities such as Galați, Sibiu, Iași, Tulcea, Brǎila, or Constanța. “So far, no calls have been received through the 112 emergency service, and no property damage or casualties have been reported,” Romania’s General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations (IGSU) said shortly after the earthquake. “Operational crews are in the field conducting reconnaissance missions.” https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=1557423473095652&set=a.252691593568853 Meanwhile, Bucharest emergency crews sent a specialized vehicle to inspect the capital’s Old Town for possible damage. “At this time, an ISU Bucharest-Ilfov vehicle is conducting a reconnaissance mission in the Old Town area to identify any possible consequences,” the local emergency inspectorate said, as quoted by Agerpres . “No calls have been registered through the 112 emergency number.” IGSU also reminded the public that Romania’s RO-ALERT system does not issue warnings before earthquakes. Monday’s earthquake was the strongest recorded in Romania so far this year, according to Agerpres. The previous most significant quake was a magnitude 4.5 event recorded in Vrancea County on February 26.

data.title: Update: Romanian seventh-grader attacks teacher and classmate with knife over religion
data.description: A seventh-grade student from “Ștefan cel Mare” Middle School in Bistrița, northern Romania, allegedly attacked a teacher and a sixth-grade classmate with a knife on Monday, October 19. The sixth-grade student is in foster care and was targeted by the attacker because of his religion, according to Vasile Șteopoaie, head of the Bistrița-Năsăud County School Inspectorate (ISJ), cited by Euronews Romania . According to Vasile Șteopoaie, the student allegedly came to school with a knife and looked for a sixth-grade classmate whom he intended to attack. The attacker had returned from Spain several years ago, according to the official. The attacker, identified as A.O.T., arrived at school as usual, a few minutes before 8 AM. However, he did not go to class and instead stayed in the bathroom. After classes began, he put a balaclava over his head and a helmet on, took the knife, and posted a video on TikTok. “I’ve been preparing this for eight months! See you in Valhalla! I’m doing it! They have no idea how dangerous I am!” he announced in the video and stories he posted, cited by Digi24. The teacher allegedly blocked his access to the classroom, at which point the student allegedly struck her with the knife. He subsequently entered the classroom looking for the classmate he was targeting. Another student allegedly intervened to help his teacher and was injured, the head of the ISJ explained. The student was eventually restrained and was in police custody. Bistrita-Nasaud ISJ head noted that the minor had radicalisation tendencies, targeting the other student because he belonged to a different religion. The two victims, aged 28 and 12, were transported to the hospital in stable condition and conscious. According to the official, the investigation has been taken over by DIICOT. The circumstances of the attack and its motive are to be established by the authorities. “The Prosecutor’s Office attached to the Bistrița-Năsăud Tribunal has been notified in this case regarding the commission of attempted aggravated murder,” the Bistrița-Năsăud County Police Inspectorate said. To manage the situation, one SMURD first-aid crew, one SMURD mobile intensive care crew, one County Ambulance Service crew with a doctor, and one special vehicle for transporting personnel and multiple victims were mobilised. Classes were suspended, and the students remained under the supervision of teachers until their parents arrived to take them home.

data.title: How Poland and Ukraine are Rebuilding Trust one Grave at a Time
data.description: Ukrainian researchers uncovered the remains of approximately 30 Ukrainian civilians killed in 1944 at an Orthodox cemetery in Łasków, eastern Poland, following search permits granted by Polish authorities. The operation mirrors parallel summer excavations in Volhynia that recovered 55 Polish victims killed in 1943, marking operational progress under a bilateral dignified burials framework established in late 2024. The depoliticized system allows mutual forensic access, exhumations, and commemorative burials while insulating technical operations from ongoing political and legal disputes regarding the historical classification of wartime massacres.

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: Côte d’Ivoire : derrière l’excédent de 369 milliards, 6 100 milliards d’emprunts
data.description: Abidjan annonce un budget 2025 bouclé sur un excédent de trésorerie. Mais ses propres documents budgétaires et le dernier rapport de la Banque mondiale racontent une autre histoire : un déficit de près de 2 000 milliards, des emprunts massifs, une dette qui avale l’essentiel des recettes et un déficit qui repart à la hausse. Le 14 octobre 2026, le Conseil des ministres ivoirien a adopté le projet de loi de règlement du budget de l’État pour l’exercice 2025. Selon le porte-parole du gouvernement, Amadou Coulibaly, les ressources, « y compris les comptes spéciaux du Trésor », ont été recouvrées […]

data.title: Minister Currie wil leerlingen met taalachterstand eerst Nederlands leren
data.description: Kinderen die onvoldoende Nederlands spreken, moeten volgens onderwijsminister Dirk Currie eerst de kans krijgen hun taalvaardigheid te verbeteren voordat zij doorstromen naar het reguliere onderwijs. Het ministerie wil nog dit schooljaar een speciaal taaltraject beginnen. Vooral leerlingen uit het binnenland en kinderen afkomstig uit het buitenland hebben volgens de minister te maken met taalachterstanden die hun schoolprestaties kunnen beïnvloeden. The post Minister Currie wil leerlingen met taalachterstand eerst Nederlands leren appeared first on Suriname Herald .

data.title: Sekteleider in Kenia schuldig aan uithongering van 190 kinderen
data.description: De Keniaanse sekteleider Paul Mackenzie is schuldig bevonden aan het uithongeren van 190 kinderen en één volwassene. Hij overtuigde ouders ervan hun kinderen te laten verhongeren om Jezus eerder te ontmoeten. Zelfs een pasgeboren baby kreeg geen borstvoeding en overleed na twaalf dagen. data.title: Simons wil dat Nederland meebetaalt aan opleiding Surinaamse verpleegkundigen
data.description: “Als je verpleegkundigen nodig hebt uit Suriname, dan moet je ons komen helpen om ze op te leiden hier.” Met die boodschap wil president Jennifer Simons Nederland betrekken bij de opleiding van Surinaams zorgpersoneel. Zij heeft het voorstel besproken met premier Rob Jetten. Tijdens de start van een opleiding voor 175 verpleegkundigen bij het AZP maakte Simons duidelijk dat zij blijft streven naar afspraken over opleiding, werkervaring en terugkeer naar Suriname. The post Simons wil dat Nederland meebetaalt aan opleiding Surinaamse verpleegkundigen appeared first on Suriname Herald .
